**`install-single` IS BROUGHT TO PARITY WITH `install`, AND WHAT THAT COST WAS
NOT PRECISION: IT WAS SIX UPSTREAM SIGNATURES AND A THREADING LAYER NOBODY HAD
COUNTED.** [M-217](#m-217) recorded that the single install differs from the
double one in **six** ways, two structural and three incidental, and named
closing the incidental three as the next step. Closing them found a **seventh**,
and the seventh is the one that changes answers.

**THE SEVENTH IS THAT PARDISO WAS ON A DIFFERENT MKL.** Read out of the two
CMake caches rather than remembered:

| | `install` | `install-single`, before |
|---|---|---|
| `MKL_PARDISO_LIBRARIES` | `/opt/intel/oneapi/mkl/latest/lib/` `libmkl_core` + `libmkl_intel_lp64` + **`libmkl_gnu_thread`** | `.../lib/intel64/` `libmkl_core` + `libmkl_intel_lp64` + **`libmkl_sequential`** |
| `CUDA_ARCH` | `sm_75` | **`sm_60`**, the cache default, wrong for this card |

PARDISO is the default trace solver, so this is not a build detail — it is the
one [M-78](#m-78) measured as deciding *which problems converge* on a knife
edge. **And no list of `MFEM_USE_*` flags contains it**, which is why it
survived a section written entirely in terms of those flags. `CLAUDE.md`'s
*Traps* entry predicted exactly this — *"a fresh configure re-searches for what
a long-lived build directory was given by hand"* — and it is now a measurement
rather than a warning.

**THE REFERENCE'S `MKL_SEQUENTIAL` COMPONENT POINTS AT `libmkl_gnu_thread`,
BY HAND.** `FindMKL_PARDISO.cmake` declares a component literally named
`MKL_SEQUENTIAL`, and `install`'s cache carries
`MKL_PARDISO_MKL_SEQUENTIAL_LIBRARY = .../libmkl_gnu_thread.so`. **That is not
recoverable from any documented knob** — `MKL_PARDISO_DIR` and
`MKL_LIBRARY_DIR` alone resolve `mkl_core` and `mkl_intel_lp64` out of Debian's
`/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` and the component to `mkl_sequential`. Reaching the
reference took pinning all three `FILEPATH` entries and `MKL_PARDISO_INCLUDE_DIR`
explicitly. *A cache entry set by hand years ago is not a configuration anybody
can re-derive; copy it, and diff it token by token afterwards.*

**AND SUNDIALS HAS TO BE BUILT SINGLE TOO, WHICH MFEM DOES NOT CHECK.** There is
no guard anywhere relating `SUNDIALS_PRECISION` to `real_t`;
`mfem::SundialsNVector` simply fails much later where a `real_t *` meets a
`sunrealtype *`. `../sundials/cuda-single-install` is 7.5.0 at
`-DSUNDIALS_PRECISION=SINGLE`, otherwise matching `cuda-install`.

**AND MFEM ITSELF DOES NOT COMPILE IN THAT PAIRING — SIX SIGNATURES, AND THE
FIRST FILE TO MEET THEM IS `linalg/batched/native.cpp` AT 11%.** `CVODESolver::
Step`, `CVODESSolver::Step` and `CVODESSolver::StepB` spell their time arguments
`double` where `ODESolver::Step` spells them `real_t`, plus three definitions;
then twelve more sites in `sundials.cpp` — `SundialsNVector`'s two constructors,
`SetData`, `SetDataAndSize`, `EvalQuadIntegration`, its `B` sibling, the
host/device array pointers and two `hinused, hlast, hcur, tcur` blocks. `ARKStep`
and `IDA` already say `real_t`, so this is **two classes that were missed rather
than a convention**. Reported as
`../mfem-hdg-dev/doc/HDG-SUNDIALS-SINGLE-PRECISION-FROM-MEQ.md`.

**THE SUITE READS 46 RED OF 63 AGAINST THE PARITY INSTALL, UP FROM 44, AND
NOTHING WENT GREEN — WHICH IS THE THIRD TIME THIS CAMPAIGN THAT THE COUNT HAS
BEEN THE WRONG INSTRUMENT.** What the install bought is visible only in the
composition, because **a test that aborted at its first case now runs every
case**:

| | error lines, before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `SourceViewTests` | 15 | **436** |
| `DeviceRowsTests` | 4 | **272** |
| `NewtonConvergence` | 12 | **41** |
| `FreeBoundaryCoupling` | 18 | **39** |
| `HighBetaConvergence` | 1 | **19** |

Every *"MFEM was built without `MFEM_USE_SUNDIALS`"* and every *"no Device is
configured"* is gone; `DeviceRowsTests` now RUNS the kernel and reports
`device 1.25095053e+09 against host 1250950355.6772461` — a real disagreement
where it previously reported a refusal. **A suite that refuses is not a suite
that fails, and a red count cannot tell them apart.**

**THE TWO NEW REDS ARE NOT THE INSTALL BREAKING ANYTHING, AND BOTH WERE
ATTRIBUTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.**

**`cuDSSTraceSolver` IS MEQ'S OWN PORT DEFECT, AND IT IS A LESSON ABOUT WHAT A
SWEEP CAN SEE.** It reports `cuDSS vs UMFPACK: worst relative difference
9.069e+300`, which is `‖x‖` over a `1.0e-300` guard against a reference of
exactly zero. M-217 guarded the PARDISO-vs-UMFPACK contraction on
`MFEM_USE_SUITESPARSE` and did not guard the cuDSS one — **because cuDSS was off
in the single install of that day, so the block did not compile at all**. The
same configuration hid the **fourteenth** of that session's thirteen
`std::max( 1.0e-300, ‖x‖ )` division guards, at `TraceSolverScaling.cpp:503`.
*A sweep of the compiled tree is a sweep of one configuration's preprocessor
output*, and `std::max`'s type deduction found the fourteenth the moment the
`#ifdef` opened.

**`MachineFixedBoundary` IS A COIN TOSS, AND `MKL_NUM_THREADS=1` IS THE DRAW
`ctest` PINS.** `examples/fixed-h-circular.toml` exits 2. Swept with the one
perturbation that reassociates a blocked BLAS-3 and changes nothing else —
[M-186](#m-186)'s instrument, applied to one binary rather than two:

| `MKL_NUM_THREADS` | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| exit | **2** | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Newton steps | did not converge in 80 | 12 | 11 | 12 |
| final `‖r‖/‖r₀‖` | 6.48e-01 | 1.28e-05 | 5.41e-05 | 1.28e-04 |

Three of four converge, in 11 to 12 steps. So the case is **marginal in single
and its success is decided by a summation order**, which is a property of the
problem in this format and not of the install — and the same statement M-186
made about `XPointBorder` and M-78 about `PedestalConvergence`, now for a third
case and a third reason.

**WHAT THE TOLERANCE WORK IS WORTH, AND THE FIRST ONE IS THE CLEANEST RESULT IN
THIS SECTION.**

**A CENTRAL DIFFERENCE AT A FIXED STEP ACCUSED THE JACOBIAN OF ITS OWN
CANCELLATION.** `NewtonConvergence` and `RotatingNewtonConvergence` difference
the assembled residual at `step = 1.0e-5` and assert agreement below `1.0e-8`.
The two error terms are `O( step² )` truncation and `O( eps/step )`
cancellation, so `eps/step` is **2.2e-11 in double and 1.2e-02 in single** — and
the eight measured directions read:

| | dir 0 | dir 1 | dir 2 | dir 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NewtonConvergence`, before | 1.524e-02 | 1.999e-02 | 2.372e-02 | 1.705e-02 |
| `RotatingNewtonConvergence`, before | 1.809e-02 | 1.656e-02 | 2.139e-02 | 1.568e-02 |
| **after**, at `cbrt( eps )` | **5.292e-05** | **4.378e-05** | **4.719e-05** | **4.250e-05** |
| **after**, rotating | **4.220e-05** | **3.708e-05** | **3.730e-05** | **4.768e-05** |

`eps/step` to the figure before, and `eps^(2/3)` = 2.4e-05 to the figure after.
**A factor of 400 on the measured quantity, and the Jacobian had not moved by a
bit.** `meq::tests::jacobianDifferenceStep()` and
`jacobianDifferenceTolerance()` are one shared pair, M-189's rule applied to a
step and the tolerance it entitles: *moving one without the other is how a
difference that cannot be resolved gets asserted against a bound that assumed it
could.*

**AND AN ABSOLUTE L2 CEILING IS A RELATIVE ONE WITH THE SCALE LEFT OUT.** Every
ceiling in `tests/convergence/` was set at about three times a measured
double-precision error, so each is `3C h^(k+1) |psi|` with the `|psi|` folded
into the digits — fine while discretisation limits the error, and meaningless
once it does not. `SolovievConvergence` reads 1.08e-05 at `k = 2` and 7.60e-06
at `k = 3` against ceilings that fall by 340 between them. `checkOrder()` now
floors both ceilings, and `meq::GradShafranovSolver::exactPotentialNorm()` /
`exactFluxNorm()` supply the denominator **in the same measure and on the same
quadrature rule** the errors are taken in.

**AND THE CONSTANT IS 2048, MEASURED AGAINST THE DOUBLE BUILD ON THE SAME
WORKING TREE** — the only control that separates a format's floor from a
method's error. The worst `‖error‖ / ( eps ‖exact‖ )` over the sequences in this
directory is **1412**, `Solov'ev NSTX` in the flux at `k = 3` on the finest
mesh, so the margin is 1.45. Thin for a discriminator and ample for a ceiling:
what a ceiling exists to catch is a solution wrong by a constant factor, a sign
or a convention, and those are `O( ‖exact‖ )` errors, seven orders above this.
**It cannot reach the double build**, which was checked: `2048 eps_double ‖q‖`
is `1.1e-12` on the largest `‖q‖` in the directory (2.398) against a tightest
historical ceiling of `6.6e-10`.

**A RATE BETWEEN TWO ERRORS AT THE FLOOR IS NOT A RATE, AND `k+1` ABOVE
`k = 1` IS A DOUBLE-BUILD ACCEPTANCE.** `FieldConvergence` reported `B converged
at -1.06` and `-1.41`, `Solov'ev NSTX` at `k = 3` reports `-0.62`, `-1.67`,
`-1.10`; those are solvers that have already arrived, not solvers converging
badly. Against the double build, single divided by double, in the flux:

| | `n = 4` | `n = 8` | `n = 16` | `n = 32` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `k = 1` | 1.00× | 1.00× | 1.00× | **1.09×** |
| `k = 2` | 1.00× | 1.05× | **6.9×** | **203×** |
| `k = 3` | **1.50×** | **36×** | **1793×** | **61,000×** |

At `k = 1` every mesh is clean and every pair reports 1.87 to 1.99. At `k = 2`
exactly one pair of three survives. At `k = 3` the **coarsest** mesh is already
1.5× contaminated, so there is no window: coarsening leaves the asymptotic
regime and refining goes deeper into round-off.

**THREE PER-PAIR CRITERIA WERE TRIED AND MEASURED, AND ALL THREE FAILED — THAT
IS THE FINDING.** A floor of `C · eps · ‖q‖ ·` (trace dofs) puts
`k = 1, n = 32` — 9% contaminated, reporting a good 1.873 — at **0.277** and
`k = 3, n = 8` — 36× contaminated — at **0.249**, and **no constant separates
them**. A constant-free *"the error must at least halve"* is a weak necessary
condition and correctly drops the flattened rows, but `MaschkePerrin` at
`k = 3` has a pair that halves comfortably and still reports **3.03** against a
wanted 3.85 — partially contaminated, genuinely converging, and not at `k+1`.
Asserting on the **best** pair does not save it either, because that *is* the
best pair. **The tail bends before it flattens**, so nothing local to a pair can
tell a degraded rate from a measured one.

**SO THE SKIP IS BY DEGREE, WHICH IS HONEST RATHER THAN TUNED.** A single build
verifies `k+1` at `k = 1` and, above that, verifies the **absolute** error
against a floored ceiling instead, saying in the run which degree it gave up on
and why. Nothing is left unable to fail: a solution wrong by a constant factor,
a sign or a convention is `O( ‖exact‖ )` and is exactly what the ceiling
catches, with seven orders of margin.

**THE ALTERNATIVE WOULD HAVE BEEN TO WIDEN `rateSlack` UNTIL THE TABLES
PASSED**, and that is the vacuity `CLAUDE.md`'s testing stance forbids: it
weakens the assertion on every mesh in **every** build — including the ones
still measuring the method — to accommodate meshes that are not. *A build that
cannot measure something should say so, not measure it loosely.*

**AND THE FLOOR MACHINERY IS ITS OWN HEADER BECAUSE FOUR OF THE FIVE STUDIES
THAT NEED IT DO NOT INCLUDE THE HARNESS.** `SolovievConvergence`,
`ExtensionConvergence`, `EstimatorConvergence` and `RotatingSourceConvergence`
each carry their own `Measurement`, their own `rate()`, their own `printTable()`
and — until this section — **their own copy of the same six-line ceiling
assertion**. A floor added where only `ConvergenceHarness.hpp` could reach it
would have floored one of four call sites and left three reporting a format as a
method. `tests/convergence/RoundOffFloor.hpp` is the one implementation, and
`FloorCheck` is a POD rather than a `Measurement` for the same reason: a helper
taking `meq::tests::Measurement const &` reaches exactly one of the five
structs. **This is [M-165](#m-165) and [M-189](#m-189) for a third time**, and
the tell was the same both previous times — a constant, or here a construction,
kept in step by hand across N sites.

**AND A BLANKET SWEEP OF SUB-EPSILON LITERALS WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG 102 TIMES.**
`tests/` carries **335** assertion literals below FP32's 1.19e-07. Split by
whether the test is red in single:

| | count |
|---|---|
| in tests that are RED | 233 |
| **in tests that are GREEN** | **102** |

The 102 are `SourceFactoryTests` (24), `ConfigTests` (20), `ExteriorDtNTests`
(17), `CoilsTests` (11), `SafetyFactorTests` (8) and their kind — **the
MFEM-free half**, where `Config`, `Profiles`, `Source`, `SourceFactory` and
`Coil` stay `double` in both builds by the *Layout* decision. Their 1e-13
assertions are correct as written and a sweep would have loosened every one.
*The design decision that makes the port small is the same one that makes the
mechanical sweep wrong*, and §7.2 proposed exactly that sweep.

**THE RESULT, AND THE COUNT IS STILL THE WRONG INSTRUMENT.** Single reads
**40 red of 63** against the parity install's 46, with **157** distinct failing
cases against 173. Six tests cleared and none regressed:
`SolovievConvergence`, `FieldConvergence`, `RotatingSolovievConvergence`,
`RotatingSourceConvergence`, `MaschkePerrinConvergence` and `cuDSSTraceSolver`.

**AND THE DOUBLE CONTROL IS 62/63 THROUGHOUT**, the one red being the standing
deliberate `PlasmaEdgeConvergence` — checked after every change, not at the end:
two new solver accessors, a shared FD step and its tolerance, a floored ceiling
at five call sites, a rate skip at five more, and a floored tracer tolerance
moved **nothing** in double. That is what the `std::max` and `#ifdef`
construction is for, and it is the only reason any of this could be attempted on
the shared tree rather than on a branch.

**WHAT IS LEFT IS 157 CASES AND IT IS A CAMPAIGN, NOT A STEP.** The largest
remaining groups are `FreeBoundaryCoupling` (17), `DriverAcceptance` (18) and
`FluxSurfaceConvergence` (12), and they are not tolerance work: the first meets
an `MFEM_VERIFY` on a geometric predicate inside MFEM, the second reads element
counts that differ by one after a marking decision moved, and the third is the
tracer and the fits. **`SourceViewTests` (7) cannot be repaired by a tolerance
at all** — it pins the device POD to the **bit** against MEQ's MFEM-free
`Source`, which is `real_t` against `double` **by design**, so the design
decision that makes the port small is the one that puts a format boundary
through MEQ's most load-bearing unit test.

### M-219

**ELEVEN SINGLE-PRECISION TESTS, AND IN EVERY ONE THE CLAIM SURVIVED THE FORMAT
WHILE THE WAY IT WAS MEASURED DID NOT.** [M-218](#m-218) left 40 red of 63 at
157 distinct failing cases and named the rate class as dominant. Working down
from the tests with fewest failing cases, the pattern that emerges is sharper
than "tolerances need scaling": **each of these was asserting something that is
true in double and is an ARTEFACT of double there** — an iteration count, a
bit-equality, a threshold with no scale in it, an order estimate that needs
fifteen decades. The repair is to assert the claim directly, which in several
cases is a *stronger* test than the one it replaces.

**THE REDUCTION AND NOT THE COUNT.** *"Newton takes one step on a source that
does not depend on psi"* is evidence for *"the Jacobian is the derivative of the
residual"*, and the count is decided by where `solve()`'s target sits.
`SolovievGeometryConvergence`, `‖r₁‖/‖r₀‖`:

| | Example 1 FRC | Example 2 ITER | Example 3 NSTX | Newton stops at |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| double | 1.29e-13 | 3.62e-14 | 1.26e-13 | **1** |
| single | 6.42e-05 | 2.10e-05 | 5.87e-05 | **2** |
| double, in its own `eps` | 580 | 163 | 566 | |
| single, in its own `eps` | 539 | 176 | 493 | |

**The same number.** The Jacobian is exactly as exact in single as in double and
the iteration count says otherwise. And the replacement is stronger: a merely
close Jacobian would still stop at one iteration under a loose enough target,
and could not reach `8192 eps` in one step.

**A RATIO WHOSE DENOMINATOR MOVES NEEDS A DIFFERENT BOUND FROM ONE WHOSE DOES
NOT, AND `MillerConvergence` HAD ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN WHY**: *"‖r₁‖ sits at
round-off while ‖r₀‖ shrinks with the mesh, so the ratio grows even though the
step is exact throughout"*. Over that sweep the drop runs 4.8e-13 → 3.1e-11 in
double and 2.7e-04 → 4.3e-03 in single — **in each build's own `eps`, 1.4e5 and
3.6e4**, so the single build is the better behaved of the two, and the caller's
historical `1.0e-8` is itself **4.5e7 eps**.

**A ROOT RESIDUAL IS A THRESHOLD WITH SEVEN ORDERS IN IT AND THE FLOOR EATS
FOUR.** `CriticalPointConvergence` states its own yardstick — *"a point reported
at `|q| = 1e-3` is a place Newton gave up"* — against a bound of `1.0e-10`.
Measured in single: the axis reaches `4.28e-07` and **the X-point `7.77e-06`**,
a saddle being worse conditioned than an extremum. `256 eps` is `3.05e-05`,
clearing the worst by 3.9 and still **33 times** below the `1e-3` that means the
search gave up.

**AND THE ROBUST HALF OF A RATE CLAIM SURVIVES WHERE THE `k+1` HALF DOES NOT.**
`theXPointConvergesAtTheFluxesOwnOrder` asserts both that the position rate
equals the **field's own** rate and that it reaches `k+1`. The first compares the
finder against the field it roots, so both sides degrade together and it holds at
any precision; only the second is skipped. *Keeping them apart is the point, and
a test that asserts two things at once hides which one the format took.*

**AN ORDER ESTIMATE NEEDS DECADES AND SINGLE HAS HALF OF THEM.** A quadratic run
in double spans `1 → 1e-4 → 1e-8 → 1e-15` — four residuals, two clean triples;
in single it is `1 → 1e-4 → 1e-7` and stops. `RotatingNewtonConvergence` reads
**1.796** against a threshold of 1.8, and `VaryingCentrifugalConvergence` reads
**0**, because `bestNewtonOrder()` correctly finds no triple above the floor. The
discriminator is quadratic against linear and that file measures its own
5%-inconsistent control at **1.173**, so 1.5 sits between 1.17 and 1.80 with room
on both sides.

**AND ONE CASE IS A DOUBLE-BUILD ACCEPTANCE OUTRIGHT, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN
THREE TUNED CONSTANTS.** `aPerturbedJacobianCostsNewtonItsOrderAndNotItsAnswer`
is a controlled experiment measuring a DIFFERENCE between an exact Jacobian and
a 5% wrong one: an order falling 1.792 → 1.173, one extra Newton iteration, and
an `L2( psi )` that does not move. In single `bestNewtonOrder()` returns **0 for
both arms**, so the gap it asks for is zero by construction; the perturbed run
takes no extra iteration because the target was already met; and the two
`L2( psi )` agree to 1e-3 rather than 1e-6 because both are AT the floor and
differ by it. **Loosening the three bounds until they passed would leave a case
that cannot tell a 5% Jacobian error from an exact one — which is the only thing
it exists to do — and it would leave that case looking green.**

**A DIFFERENCE IS NOT A DERIVATIVE AND ITS ERROR IS `sqrt( eps )`.** Where two
routes to a quantity are both exact, `eps` is the right floor; where one is a
finite difference it is not. `HighBetaConvergence`'s corner route, assembled
against differenced, relative: `2.56e-05` and `1.77e-04` at `n = 8`, `1.83e-05`
and `6.91e-05` at `n = 16` — exactly the band between `eps^(2/3)` = 2.44e-05 and
`sqrt( eps )` = 3.45e-04. **And this floor applies in single ONLY**, because
`sqrt( eps_double )` is `1.49e-08`, *larger* than the `1.0e-8` these callers ask
for: a `std::max` there would loosen the double build, which is the one thing
none of this may do.

**THE LOAD-BEARING ONE IS `SourceViewTests` AND IT NEEDED THREE DIFFERENT
REPAIRS.** Its stated justification for bit-equality is that the two expressions
evaluate *"the same arithmetic in the same order on the same **doubles**"*, and
under `MFEM_PRECISION = single` that premise is false — the POD returns
`mfem::real_t` and `meq::Source` stays `double` by the *Layout* decision.
`exactAgreementFloor()` returns **exactly zero in double**, so the bit-equality
is untouched there.

**THE OTHER TWO WERE NOT ROUND-OFF AT ALL, AND BOTH ARE PROPERTIES OF THE POD.**
`meq::KnotView::psi` is `real_t` while `meq::Profile`'s abscissae are `double`,
so the interval **boundary** moves by an ulp. Probed at the failing point:

| four ulps below | the POD | the profile | four ulps above |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 3.8925e-05 | 1.1122e-05 | 2.0352e-03 |

The two do not disagree about the function; they evaluate a rapidly varying one
a few ulps apart, and every value in that range is one it legitimately takes.
**The same thing happens one level up at a coil edge**: the file's coils are
`[1.85, 2.15]` and `[1.90, 2.20]` and its sweep visits `R = 2.20` on purpose,
because — in its own words — *"`contains()` is closed and a half-open POD would
differ"*. There the POD reports **-9.2153** where the reference reports **0**:
not a rounding difference but the whole coil term, switched on or off by which
side of its own edge the point fell. Asking that the POD lie in the range the
reference takes within a few ulps keeps every defect the file hunts — a dropped
`mu0` is a factor of 1.3e-06 and lands outside that bracket at **every** point,
not at one.

**AND ONE CONTRACT IS GENUINELY NARROWED, WHICH IS RECORDED RATHER THAN TIDIED.**
`DeviceRowsTests` pins `meq::DeviceRows` to `meq::CompressedRows` *to the bit*,
and that contract is about REASSOCIATION — MEQ refuses `reduction( + : )` so the
answer cannot depend on a thread count. But `CompressedRows` stores
`std::vector<double>` and `DeviceRows` stores `mfem::real_t`, so in single they
differ **by the format before any question of order arises**, and no edit to the
kernel could make bit-equality hold. What survives at `1024 eps` is the layout —
a transposed `r + nr*c`, a wrong support index, a dropped row, all `O( 1 )`
relative. **The reassociation half is now a double-build acceptance.** Making it
hold in both would mean giving `CompressedRows` the same `real_t` its mirror
carries: bit-identical in double, and nobody has measured it in single.

**THE RESULT.** Single reads **29 red of 63** against M-218's 40, at **125**
distinct failing cases against 157 — eleven tests green and none regressed: `SolovievGeometryConvergence`, `BorderAssembly`,
`BorderJacobian`, `CriticalPointConvergence`, `SourceViewTests`,
`DeviceRowsTests`, `DeviceQuadratureTests`, `RotatingNormalisedConvergence`,
`RotatingNewtonConvergence`, `VaryingCentrifugalConvergence` and
`HighBetaConvergence`. **The double control is 62/63 throughout**, which is not
a courtesy check here but the thing that makes the work possible at all: every
helper either `std::max`es against the caller's own historical value or is
`#ifdef`'d, so a misapplied guard cannot weaken the double build and the control
says so.


### M-220

**THE SINGLE-PRECISION FLOORS ARE NOT ALL `eps`, AND THE FOUR THAT ARE NOT ARE
THE FINDING.** [M-219](#m-219) took single from 40 red of 63 to 29, on one
distinction — *a difference is not a derivative*, so the floor is `eps` where
both routes are exact and `eps^(2/3)` to `sqrt( eps )` where one is a finite
difference. Working down the remaining 125 cases turns up three more laws, each
measured rather than assumed, and together they cover most of what was left.

**A TOLERANCE A SOLVER WAS GIVEN IS THE FLOOR ON WHAT IT CAN ACHIEVE, AND SEVEN
SITES NAMED A LITERAL INSTEAD.** Every one asks
`newtonResiduals().back() < 1.0e-08` while handing `solve()` a target built by
`meq::newtonTolerance()`, which floors at ten `eps` — `1.19e-06` in single. So
the solve reaches exactly what it was asked for and the test rejects it at a
hundred times tighter. M-217's lesson one level out: *a default is only a
default on the paths that do not override it*, and here the override is in the
caller. The same shape appears in the tracer, where `Contour::correctorTarget`
reads `1.12e-12` in double and `1.335e-06` in single and the worst residual
achieved is `3.07e-10` and **exactly `1.335e-06`** — the corrector meeting its
target in both, against assertions of `1.0e-08` and `1.0e-09` chosen when the
target was `1e-12`.

**AND A FIXED-POINT ITERATION CANNOT BE ASKED FOR A NEWTON'S TOLERANCE.** This
is the sharpest of the four and it is a statement about the METHOD rather than
about any constant. Newton's last step squares the residual, so a target within
an order of the arithmetic's own floor is met on the step that crosses it.
Picard contracts by a fixed factor, approaches the floor from above and never
crosses it — and Anderson acceleration makes this worse rather than better,
since the least-squares combination it forms over the difference history is a
cancellation of vectors that are themselves at round-off. Measured on
`NewtonConvergence`'s Example 5 at `k = 2, n = 16`:

| path | double | single, target `1.19e-06` | single, target `4.88e-04` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Newton | 3 iterations | 3 iterations | 3 iterations |
| Anderson–Picard | converges | **500 iterations, stalled at `5.80e-05`** | converges |
| Picard, `w = 0.5` | converges | not reached — the case aborts above | converges |
| Picard → Newton | converges | not reached — the case aborts above | converges |

`meq::picardTolerance()` is the repair: `4096 eps` in single and **the caller's
own value in double**, `#ifdef`'d rather than `std::max`'d because `4096 eps` in
double is `9.1e-13` and `FreeBoundaryCoupling` asks for `1.0e-13` — a scaled
version would loosen that build rather than leave it alone.

**IT DOES NOT CURE `pedestalSelfConverges`, AND THAT NEGATIVE IS WORTH KEEPING.**
That case went green on two targeted runs afterwards and red again on the full
`-j4` suite, at *"k = 1, h = 0.0333: Newton did NOT converge in 60 iterations"* —
which is the **same** case `pedestalConvergenceIsAResolutionThreshold` spends
forty lines establishing as a knife edge decided by a threaded BLAS-3's
summation order at `O( 1e-16 )`, and which [M-186](#m-186) measured failing in
two of five thread configurations on `HEAD` itself. *A case that changes verdict
between two runs of one binary is not evidence about a change made between
them.*

**AND IT IS NOT THE COMPENSATED SUMMATION HINT, WHICH WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN
ASSUMED.** SUNDIALS 7.5.0 has compensated sums, and they are an **ARKODE SPRK**
runtime option — `ARKodeSetUseCompensatedSums()`, `arkode.c:2763`, reached from
`ark_kepler.c --use-compensated-sums` — for the time accumulation of a
symplectic stepper. There is no `SUNDIALS_BUILD_WITH_COMPENSATED_SUMS` in
`cmake/SundialsBuildOptions*.cmake`, and `src/kinsol/` contains the string
nowhere. So a rebuild of `../sundials/cuda-single-install` could not have
reached this, and the KINSOL stall is the method meeting the format rather than
a summation that could be made exact.

**A STATIONARY POINT'S POSITION COSTS HALF THE DIGITS, AND ITS VALUE COSTS
NONE.** Near a maximum `psi = psi_max − c dz²`, so a flux known to `eps` pins
the position only to `sqrt( eps/c )` — `3.45e-04` in single against `1.49e-08`
in double, four and a half orders apart where the format is one, and no
refinement moves it. Measured, `LimiterCurve`'s located contact stands
1.177e-03, 2.408e-04, **1.536e-04** from the midplane over `n = 12, 24, 48`:
converging at 2.289 on the first pair and then flooring, at `sqrt( eps )` on a
half-width of 0.5. `AxisAgreement`'s located axis reads `R = 0.99999583` against
an exact 1 and `z = −3.16e-06` against 0, both asserted against `1.0e-08`.
**The other half is why this is not a loss**: the same flatness that hides the
position makes `psi` there accurate to `eps`, so an `O( sqrt( eps ) )` error in
WHERE costs `O( eps )` in the VALUE — which is the envelope argument
`LimiterCurve` already rests on, arriving from the other side.

**AN ESTIMATOR DIFFERENTIATES, SO ITS FLOOR RISES AS THE MESH FALLS — THE
OPPOSITE DIRECTION TO THE ERROR IT ESTIMATES.** `eta_1` is
`h_K || f + Delta* psi_h ||_K` and that residual is a cancellation of second
derivatives, so its round-off part carries a NEGATIVE power of `h` where every
term it is compared against carries a positive one. The two therefore cross,
and past the crossing refining makes `eta` larger. `EstimatorConvergence` at
`k = 3`, the same four meshes in both builds:

| `h` | 0.2 | 0.1 | 0.05 | 0.025 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `eta`, single | 8.93e-05 | 9.73e-05 | 1.97e-04 | **3.93e-04** |

The double build's own finest-mesh reading at that degree is **1.927e-08**, the
value `everyComponentConvergesAtKPlusOne`'s ceiling was set from, and its column
falls at `k+1` across the sequence. The single column RISES, and doubles with
each halving of `h`, so the floor goes as `1/h` here; `meq::tests::residualEstimatorFloor()` carries it. **One derivative
further on it is `1/h²`**: a flux-surface average is a quadrature over a traced
level set whose arc-length metric comes off `q`, and
`SurfaceAverageConvergence`'s rms relative error in `V'` at `k = 2` RISES
6.64e-06, 8.80e-06, 1.54e-04, **3.31e-04** over `n = 12` to 96 — a factor of 50
over an eight-fold refinement, which is `h^-1.9`. Against `eps/h²` those four
readings are 0.39, 0.13, 0.36 and 0.30 of it, so the law fits to within a factor
of three across the sweep.

**AND THAT CROSSING IS WHY AN ADAPTIVE LOOP IN A NARROW FORMAT STOPS BEING A
DESCENT.** `AdaptiveRefinement`'s uniform-marking arm, the same loop in both
builds:

| cycle | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `L2( q )`, double | 1.24e-04 | 1.58e-05 | 2.00e-06 | 2.51e-07 | 3.14e-08 |
| `L2( q )`, single | 1.23e-04 | 1.68e-05 | 1.31e-05 | **5.57e-05** | 3.05e-05 |
| elements, single | 32 | 128 | 512 | 1618 | 4567 |

The marker stops marking everything at cycle 2 — 209 of 512 — because the
indicator is now round-off and round-off is not uniform, and from there neither
`eta` nor the true error is monotone. **It is not the estimator failing**: the
estimator is reporting what the arithmetic gives it, and refining past the
crossing genuinely raises the error, the conditioning growing like `h^-2` while
the truncation falls like `h^(k+1)`.

**A PER-READING CUT IS RIGHT FOR A COMPARISON WHERE A PER-DEGREE CUT IS RIGHT
FOR A RATE, AND M-218 SETTLED ONLY THE SECOND.** That finding — that no per-pair
criterion separates a good rate from a contaminated one, because the tail bends
before it flattens — is about a rate ACROSS A SEQUENCE. *"`psi*` beats `psi_h`
by ten times"* is a different question: it is about two numbers, and it is
answerable exactly while both are above the floor. `NewtonConvergence`'s
Example 5 in single shows why the distinction pays:

| `h` | 0.2 | 0.1 | 0.05 | 0.025 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `L2( psi* )`, `k = 1` | 4.097e-03 | 4.800e-04 | 5.807e-05 | 7.235e-06 |
| rate | — | 3.093 | 3.047 | 3.005 |
| `L2( psi* )`, `k = 3` | 3.950e-06 | 1.859e-06 | 1.836e-06 | 1.771e-06 |
| rate | — | 1.088 | 0.017 | 0.052 |

A degree cut would throw the clean `k = 1` column away with the rest.
`aboveTheFormatsFloor()` is the predicate and it is `#ifdef`'d true in double,
so it cannot drop an assertion that build makes today.

**AND A DRIFT IS A RATIO OF RATIOS, WITH THE ROUND-OFF IN IT TWICE AND THE
SIGNAL ONCE.** `EstimatorConvergence`'s effectivity index is asserted to settle
to within 1.5 per cent between consecutive meshes, which is the sharpest
statement in that directory. At `k = 1`, its cleanest case, single reads 10.71,
10.60, 10.53, **9.66** against a double build's 10.72, 10.61, 10.55, 10.52: the
finest `L2( q )` is 9 per cent contaminated and the drift reads 0.918 against a
band of 0.95 to 1.05. The index's own bounds — reliable above, efficient below,
1 to 60 — hold at every mesh and every degree in single and are still asserted.

**THE BEST FLOOR IS ONE THE CASE MEASURES ITSELF.** `OutputConvergence`'s band
study evaluates interior nodes that are continued not at all, so whatever they
read IS the arithmetic: 8.53e-07 in single, and in double so far below the
`1.0e-12` that case asserts that it has never been the binding term. The band error
runs 1.325e-06 to 9.085e-07 over its two meshes — inside a factor of two of that
— so the "rate" of 0.54 is a rate of round-off, and the cut needs no constant at
all. `WarmStartConvergence`'s grid sweep has the same shape with a
DISCRETISATION rather than round-off as the contaminant: its own comment already
said *"by 257 nodes the grid error is within a factor of two of the coarse
solve's own, which the grid cannot represent better than"*, and in single that
gap closes enough to take the last rate from 1.735 to 1.689 against a bound of
1.7.

**TWO OF MEQ'S OWN CONSTANTS WERE WRONG AND ONE OF THEM WAS WRONG IN THE
OPPOSITE DIRECTION TO EVERY OTHER ONE IN THIS SERIES.**
`setUpDownSymmetry()`'s centroid-matching tolerance is `1e-9` of the mesh
extent; a centroid is an average of coordinates the element transformation
computes in `real_t`, so a mesh that mirrors EXACTLY hands back centroids
differing by a few `eps` of the extent — a hundred times that — and the refusal
fires on a mesh that IS symmetric. It is now `64 eps` of the extent, `7.6e-06`
in single and `1.4e-14` in double, three orders below `h/2` on the coarsest mesh
in the tree in either format.

**AND `meq::GridSampler`'s `insideTolerance` WAS TOO TIGHT BECAUSE MFEM'S OWN IS
ALREADY SCALED.** `mfem::InverseElementTransformation` carries
`ref_tol( 1e-15 ), phys_rtol( 4e-15 ), ip_tol( 1e-8 )` in double and
`ref_tol( 4e-7 ), phys_rtol( 1e-6 ), ip_tol( 1e-4 )` in single — the *opposite*
of [M-183](#m-183)'s `ExtensionBoundaryQuadrature` finding, and worth recording
as such. A floor of `128 eps` is `1.5e-05`, six times TIGHTER than what MFEM's
own inverse accepts, so MEQ's affine path refused points the Newton path took —
which is exactly the disagreement `SamplerConvergence` reported at node
`( 24, 0 )`, on the domain's bottom edge. The expression is now
`meq::samplerInsideTolerance()` in `Sampler.hpp`, MFEM's own pair copied, and
the test hands the SAME number to `SetElementTol()` before comparing the two
inverses — the M-165 rule, that a constant kept in step by hand across two
parties IS the defect.

**ONE CONTRACT NARROWS AND IT IS THE ANDERSON ARM'S.** With
`picardTolerance()` in, the three Picard paths converge and reach `L2` errors of
1.04e-04, 2.16e-04 and 2.98e-05 against Newton's 2.98e-05, where in double all
four agree to seven figures. **The solutions still agree; it is the errors that
do not** — the largest gap is 1.9e-04 on a potential of norm 6.7e-01, which is
2.8e-04 relative — and what the case exists to rule out survives untouched: the
hazard is a path landing on a DIFFERENT discrete solution, which
`CLAUDE_HDGGS.md` records at **9.4 per cent** apart, four orders above this.

**THE RESULT.** Single reads **12 red of 63** at **61** distinct failing cases,
against M-219's 29 and 125, with the double control at **62/63** — the one red
there being the standing deliberate `PlasmaEdgeConvergence`, which is therefore
one of the twelve and not a finding. Seventeen tests went green and none
regressed: `SolverContract`, `AxisConvergence`, `UpDownSymmetry`, `OpenSurfaces`,
`SurfaceFitConvergence`, `AdaptiveRefinement`, `ExtensionConvergence`,
`NewtonConvergence`, `LimiterCurve`, `WarmStartConvergence`, `AxisAgreement`,
`MillerConvergence`, `OutputConvergence`, `SamplerConvergence`,
`EstimatorConvergence`, `SurfaceAverageConvergence` and `FluxGridConvergence`.

**AND WHAT IS LEFT IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF THING, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART OF
THE COUNT.** Of the eleven that are not the deliberate red, the cases that
remain are dominated by **solves that do not converge at all** rather than by
assertions that cannot be read: `PlasmaConnectivity`, `XPointOuter`,
`DeviceParity`'s `mhd-rectangle`, `MachineFixedBoundary`'s two, and most of
`FreeBoundaryCoupling`'s 13 and `DriverAcceptance`'s 14. `MachineFixedBoundary`
is additionally the `MKL_NUM_THREADS` coin toss of [M-186](#m-186).
**The tolerance sweep `DEVICE-PLAN.md` §7.2 called the single biggest cost is
substantially done; what stands between single precision and a green suite is
now the solver and not the assertions.**

### M-221

**THE QUESTION IS NOT HOW MANY TESTS ARE RED, IT IS WHETHER THE BUILD SOLVES
ANYTHING — SO THIS MEASURES THE EXAMPLES.** [M-220](#m-220) left single at 12
red of 63, and the cases that remained were dominated by solves that do not
converge rather than by assertions that cannot be read. The instrument for that
is the shipped example tree, run in both builds at `MKL_NUM_THREADS = 1`.

**OF THE 22 EXAMPLES THAT RUN WITHOUT A MESH GENERATOR, 17 GIVE THE SAME
VERDICT IN BOTH BUILDS AND ONE FAILS IN BOTH.** The nineteen that need
`meq-run` are not in the table; `manufactured.toml` exits 1 in both and is a
standing refusal rather than a finding here.

| example | double | single | `psi_ax` single vs double |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fixed-f-diiid` | 0 | 0 | 2.897817e-01 / 2.897815e-01 — **6.9e-07** |
| `fixed-d-tcv` | 0 | 0 | 1.755690e-02 / 1.755694e-02 — 2.3e-06 |
| `fixed-e-diamagnetic` | 0 | 0 | 4.354577e-02 / 4.354586e-02 — 2.1e-06 |
| `fixed-a-testtokamak` | 0 | 0 | 4.778552e-02 / 4.778900e-02 — 7.3e-05 |
| `fixed-g-mastu` | 0 | 0 | 8.043809e-02 / 8.043321e-02 — 6.1e-05 |
| `diverted-tokamak-xpoint` | 0 | 0 | 8.266012e-02 / 8.266004e-02 — 1.0e-06 |
| `free-boundary-halfdisc` | 0 | 0 | 1.001935e-01 / 1.001931e-01 — 4.0e-06 |
| `limited-tokamak` | 0 | 0 | 9.483092e-02 / 9.484400e-02 — 1.4e-04 |
| `limiter-halfdisc` | 0 | 0 | 7.459902e-01 / 7.459870e-01 — 4.3e-06 |
| `q-driven` | 0 | 0 | 3.461169e-01 / 3.457380e-01 — 1.1e-03 |
| `rotating-normalised` | 0 | 0 | 1.039297e-01 / 1.039325e-01 — 2.7e-05 |
| `miller-curved`, `miller-adaptive`, `soloviev-nstx`, `flux-surfaces`, `rotating-rectangle`, `manufactured-driver` | 0 | 0 | no `psi_ax` reported |
| `coils-rectangle` | 0 | **1** | UMFPACK, below |
| `mhd-rectangle` | 0 | **1** | UMFPACK, below |
| `fixed-h-circular` | 0 | **2** | the coin toss, below |
| `diverted-tokamak` | 0 | **2** | root selection, below |

**THE ACCURACY IS THE CASE'S AND NOT THE FORMAT'S, OVER A RANGE OF 1,600**, from
6.9e-07 on the DIII-D machine — the largest problem in the table — to 1.1e-03 on
the `q(psi)`-driven outer loop. That is [M-204](#m-204)'s finding on two cases
widened to eleven: *a single-precision equilibrium is qualified per problem and
not per build*.

**AND `diverted-tokamak-xpoint` SOLVING WHILE `diverted-tokamak` DOES NOT IS
THE SHARPEST ROW IN THE TABLE.** They are the same machine on the same mesh. The
first puts the X-point in the border, which is XP-3; the second prescribes a
limiter at the reference X-point. So what fails is not the diverted geometry,
the free-boundary coupling, the moving support or the coil subtraction — all of
which the working row exercises — but the branch the prescribed-limiter
formulation lands on.

---

**CAUSE 1: A STRUCTURAL ABSENCE WEARING A DRIVER REFUSAL, AND IT WAS SIX
FAILING CASES.** `coils-rectangle.toml` and `mhd-rectangle.toml` pinned
`TraceSolver = "umfpack"`. UMFPACK is **double only** — SuiteSparse has no
single-precision build, which [M-217](#m-217) records as structural — so the
driver refuses, correctly and by design. The cases that fell with it were
`DriverAcceptance`'s `theDriverTakesTheConductorsOutOfTheMesh`,
`theRestartFileSaysWhatItHoldsAndWhatItIsARemainderFrom`,
`theFilamentStackMovesTowardsTheRectangleItDivides`, `theDriverAddsTheCoilsToF`
and `theDriverRefusesASolverItCannotHonour`, plus the whole of `DeviceParity`,
whose case is `mhd-rectangle`.

**NO NAMED TRACE SOLVER IS AVAILABLE IN EVERY BUILD MEQ SUPPORTS**, which is
why `meq::defaultTraceSolver()` is build-conditional: `umfpack` needs
SuiteSparse, `pardiso` needs MKL, `cudss` needs CUDA, and `gmres` is
[M-179](#m-179)'s unviable. **An example that names one is therefore
non-portable by construction**, so the two examples now name none and
`theDriverRefusesASolverItCannotHonour` names whichever this build links —
which is the question that case is really asking.

**CAUSE 2: A LOCATOR REFUSING A POINT ITS OWN FILE PRESCRIBES.**
`diverted-tokamak` died in `prepare()`, before a single Newton step, with
*"no element of the mesh contains ( 1.09314, -0.603965 )"* — the reference
X-point, written in the TOML, and located without complaint by the double
build. `mfem::ElementTransformation::TransformBack()` answers `Inside`,
`Outside` or **`Unknown`**, and the third is its own Newton failing to reach a
`phys_rtol` that `eltrans.hpp` sets to `4e-15` in double and `1e-6` in single.
A point the wide build calls `Inside`, the narrow one calls `Unknown`, and
`locatePotentialPoint()` walked past every element and threw.

It now examines the reference coordinates rather than the verdict alone, keeps
the smallest violation over the mesh, and accepts it within
`meq::samplerInsideTolerance()` — the same expression `meq::GridSampler` uses,
which is [M-165](#m-165)'s rule that a constant kept in step by hand across two
parties IS the defect. **And when it still fails the message carries the
number**, because *"no element contains it"* and *"every element missed it by
3e-07"* send a reader to two different places.

**CAUSE 3: ROOT SELECTION, WHICH IS A GENUINE LIMIT — AND THE CONTROL IS WHAT
MAKES IT ONE.** Past the locate, `diverted-tokamak` at `MKL_NUM_THREADS = 1`
reports a singular bordered Jacobian whose **plasma current row is identically
zero**. The new diagnostic says why:

```
  row 2  |row| 0.000e+00  rhs 2.513e-01
  the support edge is ( axis -8.069e-02, boundary -2.134e-02 ), span -5.935e-02
    <== NOT POSITIVE: Psi is negative everywhere, so the support is EMPTY and
        every integral over it is zero. This is not a degeneracy and
        setBorderRegularisation() will not help it
```

That is [M-165](#m-165)'s failure mode — a span of the wrong sign, and there
the loop CONVERGED to a wall-hugging annulus rather than failing. **Two controls
place it.** With `[initialguess]` removed **the double build fails
identically**, row 2 zero and the same right-hand side, so a zero current row at
a cold iterate is not a format defect. And the warm start itself is exonerated:
both builds read the stored guess as `[ -5.779358e-02, 8.076817e-02 ]` and
transfer it to `[ -5.750709e-02, 8.075919e-02 ]` against
`[ -5.750708e-02, 8.075921e-02 ]` — seven digits.

**AT 2, 4 AND 8 MKL THREADS IT CONVERGES, TO THE WRONG BRANCH.** 18 to 20
Newton steps, `psi_bnd = -1.196819e-01` against the double build's
`+3.229751e-02` and a profile scale of `5.898e-02` against `9.579e-01` — and
the driver's axis-source guard **refuses it**, naming `psi_bnd` going negative
as what chose the branch. *The safety net works; the branch does not.*

**AND `fixed-h-circular` IS [M-186](#m-186)'S COIN TOSS ONCE MORE.** It fails at
`MKL_NUM_THREADS = 1` — the value `tests/CMakeLists.txt` pins and the only one
ctest ever runs — and converges at 2, 4 and 8 in 11 to 12 iterations, reaching
`psi_ax = 6.353672e-02` against double's `6.353707e-02`. The double build's own
history on that case sits on a plateau at 5.27e-03 for three iterations with
observed orders of 0.004, 0.235 and **-0.660**, then blips UP before falling to
1.1e-16 in five: both builds are on the plateau and only one of them gets off it
at this thread count.

---

**THREE DIAGNOSTICS ARE KEPT, AND EACH IS WHAT IDENTIFIED ITS OWN CAUSE.** The
support edge and its span on a singular border; the range of the stored AND the
transferred field on a warm start, because *"0 of 31704 nodes fell outside" is a
statement about the SEARCH* and not about what was found; and the closest
element's violation on a failed locate.

**`DeviceParity` IS GREEN IN SINGLE AND THE INSTRUMENT IT CARRIES IS INTACT.**
*"`--device cuda` reproduces `--device cpu` to every printed digit"* is what
[M-79](#m-79), [M-130](#m-130) and [M-187](#m-187) were root-caused with, and it
stays an exact string comparison in double. In single the driver prints seven
significant figures of a `real_t`, which IS `eps`, so the device's summation
order moves the last one and nothing else: `psi_ax` 3.759859e-01 against
3.759861e-01, `psi_bnd` 7.081396e-02 against 7.081404e-02, the X-point 1.200931
against 1.200930. Five parts in ten million, against the **factor of two**
[M-206](#m-206) measured when a kernel was actually wrong.

**`DriverAcceptance` GOES FROM 14 FAILING CASES TO 6** and `DeviceParity` from
its whole content to none, on those three causes plus the agreement floors of
[M-220](#m-220) applied to the borders the driver reports. The double build is
unchanged throughout.

### M-222

**THE SINGLE-PRECISION SUITE IS AT PARITY WITH THE DOUBLE ONE: 62 OF 63 IN
BOTH, AND IT IS THE SAME TEST RED IN EACH** — `PlasmaEdgeConvergence`, which is
the standing deliberate red while the staircase `Γ_{p,h}` stands. Against
[M-221](#m-221)'s 11 red of 63 and [M-217](#m-217)'s 44.

| | red of 63 | distinct cases |
|---|---|---|
| [M-217](#m-217) first run | 44 | — |
| [M-218](#m-218) at install parity | 40 | 157 |
| [M-219](#m-219) | 29 | 125 |
| [M-220](#m-220) | 12 | 61 |
| [M-221](#m-221) | 11 | 52 |
| **here** | **1** | **the deliberate one** |

**AND THE DOUBLE CONTROL IS 62/63 AT EVERY STEP OF IT**, which is what the
`std::max` and `#ifdef` construction is for: a guard applied in the wrong place
cannot weaken the double build, so the sweep is safe by construction rather
than by attention.

**THE LARGEST REMAINING SINGLE-PRECISION FAILURE WAS NOT A TOLERANCE AND NOT
MEQ'S: `ElementTransformation::TransformBack`'s DEFAULT ARGUMENT IS 0.84 OF ONE
`float` EPSILON.** [M-221](#m-221) left the suite at 11 red of 63 and said what
remained was the solver. Most of it was one line of somebody else's header.

`fem/eltrans.hpp:62` carries `tol_0 = 1e-15` in double and **`1e-7` in single**,
and `IsoparametricTransformation::TransformBack` takes it as the default for
`phys_rel_tol`. Against `eps = 1.1920929e-07` that is **0.84 of one ulp**. The
double value is 4.5 eps and is reachable; the single value is not. The constant
was scaled by the ratio of the two formats' decimal digits — eight orders —
where what it has to clear is the ratio of their epsilons, 1.86e+09.

**AND IT IS TIGHTER THAN THE CLASS IT CONFIGURES**, which is what makes the
repair obvious: `InverseElementTransformation`'s own constructor carries
`phys_rtol( 4e-15 )` in double and `phys_rtol( 1e-6 )` in single, so a caller
who constructs the object gets 8.4 eps and a caller who goes through
`TransformBack()` gets 0.84.

**IT IS A WRONG VERDICT AND NOT A LOST DIGIT, BECAUSE `NewtonSolve()` HAS NO
OTHER EXIT.** For a straight-sided triangle — the whole of MEQ's meshes — the
map is affine and its inverse is one exact Newton step, and both exits are then
unreachable in single:

| exit | asks for | what an affine triangle leaves |
|---|---|---|
| `err_phys < phys_rtol*\|pt\|` | `0.84 eps*\|pt\|` | round-off, `eps*\|pt\|` |
| `dx_norm < ref_tol` | `4e-7` | `eps*\|pt\|/h`, which exceeds it for every `h` below **0.31** |

So the solve runs to `max_iter` and returns **`Unknown`** — the third answer,
which a caller testing `== Inside` reads as *not this element* for the element
the point is in.

**MEASURED, AND THE INSTRUMENT IS A COUNT RATHER THAN A CLOCK.** MEQ's
`ContourTracer` walks the mesh element by element and falls back on the
`O(elements)` `Mesh::FindPoints` when the walk fails;
`Contour::fallbackLocations` is asserted to be zero because a trace that needs
the scan is quadratic in the mesh. Three surfaces of one Solov'ev fixture at
`k = 2, n = 24`:

| `Psi_N` | double | single, `tol_0` | single, `phys_rtol = 1e-6` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.05 | 0 | **108** | 0 |
| 0.40 | 0 | **240** | 0 |
| 0.80 | 0 | **95** | 0 |

Essentially every location fell through the whole walk. **The trace still
closed**, because `FindPoints` finds the point — which is what made this a cost
rather than a failure and is why nothing but a count could see it.

**AND TWO BAND MEASUREMENTS WERE WRONG RATHER THAN SLOW.** MEQ flags a traced
point as outside the mesh by that same walk, so a point the walk could not place
was flagged extended while `Mesh::FindPoints` put it inside — 2 and 3 points of
one contour and 1 node of an angle parametrisation. **The deepest band excursion
the fixture reports moved from 2.027 h to 0.628 h** on the same mesh with only
this tolerance changed, so the band's own geometry was being read off failed
inversions.

`meq::inverseTransformTolerance()` is the repair, at MEQ's five verdict-consuming
call sites: `1e-15` in double, so every double call is bit-for-bit the call it
always was, and `1e-6` in single — upstream's own class default. It is
`meq::samplerInsideTolerance()`'s sibling with **the sign of the finding
reversed**: there upstream already scaled `ip_tol` and MEQ's own floor was six
times tighter than it, so the answer was to copy upstream's pair; here
upstream's `TransformBack` default is the thing that does not survive the
format, and copying it is what must not be done. Reported as
`HDG-TRANSFORMBACK-SINGLE-TOLERANCE-FROM-MEQ.md`.

**AND IT EXPLAINS A RESULT THIS PROJECT HAD ALREADY RECORDED AND MISATTRIBUTED.**
`PointLocator.cpp` carries a note that under `MFEM_PRECISION = single` the
default `TransformBack` lost **458 of 25616** warm-start nodes where the double
build lost none, and that retrying through a constructed
`InverseElementTransformation` with `ClosestPhysNode` recovered them. The retry
was credited to the better initial guess. It is not: constructing the object is
what buys `phys_rtol = 1e-6` instead of `1e-7`, and that alone is the cure.
*A fix that works is not an explanation of why.*

**A SECOND MFEM DEFECT OF THE SAME FAMILY IS A DISPLACEMENT BELOW ONE ULP.**
`mfem::VertexConePath` builds the transfer direction at a vertex of `Gamma_h` by
shooting a fan, averaging the nearest endpoints on `Gamma` and **differencing
that mean from the vertex**. A vertex that lies ON `Gamma` has every endpoint at
distance zero — so in single the endpoints round to the vertex itself, the
difference is the zero vector, `len <= 0` sends all three widening passes to
`continue`, and the constructor aborts with *"no ray from the vertex ... reaches
Gamma"*. Measured on `FreeBoundaryCoupling`'s circle of radius 0.40 about
`R = 1.10`: the Cartesian grid puts a vertex at `( 1.1, -0.4 )`, the circle's own
lowest point, at `phi = -2.4e-08`. **The same vertex is on `Gamma` in double
too**, and the same arithmetic works there, because a bisected crossing at
`6e-14` is still a representable displacement from a coordinate of 1.1 — a
double's ulp there is 2.2e-16 and a float's is 1.2e-07.

**`meq::markingOffset()` IS MEQ'S HALF, AND IT CLOSES A SECOND SYMPTOM NOBODY
HAD CONNECTED TO THE FIRST.** `mfem::MarkLevelSetSubdomain()` keeps an element
when `phi <= -offset` at every vertex and refined point, and every call site in
this tree passed `offset = 0` — so the set the marking decides on is exactly the
set round-off cannot decide. Besides the abort above, `DriverAcceptance` marks
one shape twice, once through the driver and once by hand, and read **451
elements against 450**: two routes building a background through different
arithmetic, which is nothing until an element straddles. The offset is exactly
zero in double, so `D_h` is the set it has always been.

**AND THE SECOND HALF OF WHAT WAS LEFT IS M-186'S COIN TOSS, ON FOUR MORE
CASES — MEASURED WITH M-186'S OWN INSTRUMENT AND NOT INFERRED FROM THE
FAILURE.** `MKL_NUM_THREADS` reassociates a blocked BLAS-3 and changes nothing
else, so the same binary run at 1, 2 and 4 separates a knife edge from a
regression. `tests/CMakeLists.txt` pins it at 1, which is the only value ctest
ever runs, and **that is one draw**:

| case | MKL = 1 | MKL = 2 | MKL = 4 | MKL = 8 | double |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pedestalSelfConverges`, `k = 1, h = 1/30` | **fails at the 60 cap** | converges | converges | — | converges |
| `fixed-h-circular` through the driver | **exits 2** | solves | solves | solves | solves |
| `PlasmaConnectivity`'s confined half | **fails at 60** | **fails at 60** | converges in 11 | — | converges in 10 |
| `XPointBorder` merit weight 4 | **195 iterations, other basin** | over the cap, skipped | — | — | converges |

**THE MERIT-WEIGHT ROW IS THE ONE THAT TAUGHT SOMETHING NEW, AND IT IS ABOUT
THE PRECONDITION RATHER THAN THE PLATEAU.** That case had skipped a weight
whose solve *did not finish*, which is how the plateau had always shown. At
`MKL = 1` in single, weight 4 finishes — in **195 bootstrap iterations against
the other three weights' 11** — and comes to rest in a NEIGHBOURING BASIN, at
`psi_ax = 8.0524e-02` and `X = ( 1.0822, -0.5973 )` against `8.2660e-02` and
`( 1.0931, -0.6035 )`. It reports `converged`. At `MKL = 2` the same weight runs
past the cap, is skipped by the precondition as written, and the case passes.

So *a run that converges is not a run that converged to your fixed point*, and
the discriminator is the **work**: eighteen times the reference weight's
iterations is not the same descent. The precondition now skips on that too, and
the separation is a factor of eighteen rather than a judgement.

**EVERY ONE OF THESE FOUR IS REPAIRED BY RELAXING A PRECONDITION AND NONE BY
RELAXING A TOLERANCE**, which is the distinction *Testing stance* turns on and
the same repair M-186 and `pedestalConvergenceIsAResolutionThreshold` already
made. Two of them are skipped **by name** — `fixed-h-circular` alone, and only
in single — so any other machine that fails still fails and a second one joining
it on the plateau would have to be measured and added rather than absorbed.

**AND WHERE THEY LAND THEY LAND ON THE RIGHT ANSWER**, which is what says the
plateau is about the route and not about the format: `PlasmaConnectivity`'s
confined solve reads `psi_ax = 1.778463e-01` in single at `MKL = 4` against
double's `1.778464e-01`, and every merit weight that descends reports `psi_ax`
to eight digits.

**THE LAWS THIS SESSION ADDS TO M-220'S FOUR ARE THREE, AND EACH IS A SIBLING
OF ONE ALREADY THERE.**

*A POSITION OBTAINED BY ROOTING CARRIES `eps`, WHERE ONE OBTAINED BY
DIFFERENCING CARRIES `eps/h`.* M-220's fourth law is about differentiated
quantities; the implicit function theorem moves a root by `dpsi/|grad psi|`, and
both factors carry the field's own size, so the mesh does not appear at all.
Measured twice: a contour's closure gap over 1, 5 and 10 circuits reads
**1.00e-07, 7.39e-07, 6.42e-07** on coordinates of 1.05, and the traced `Gamma`
settles at **4.73e-06 at k = 2 and 5.88e-06 at k = 3** — the same number at two
degrees, which is what says it is the format. 40 to 50 `eps` either way.

*AN ANSWER IS WORTH THE RESIDUAL THE SOLVER STOPPED AT, WHICH IS NOT THE ONE IT
WAS ASKED FOR.* M-220's first law says a solver cannot beat the tolerance it was
given; this is needed where it did not MEET that tolerance and returned anyway.
KINSOL stops on a step that has become too small exactly as readily as on a
function norm that has become small enough and reports `converged` for both.
`SafetyFactorSolver`'s closed-form case, asked for `1e-09` in both builds:

| | final norm | recovered `g` |
|---|---|---|
| double | 3.68e-06 | within 1e-04 |
| single | **3.71e-03** | out by **7.0e-03** |

— a factor of 1.9, which is the outer Jacobian's conditioning. And the single
figure is not KINSOL's: `q` is a flux-surface average, so the MAP's own
evaluation noise is `eps/h^2`, **6.9e-05** at that mesh, before the fit to the
coefficients of `g^2` amplifies it by a factor the two builds agree on — 106 in
double and 330 in single.

*THE FLOOR AND THE CEILING ON ONE NUMBER FAIL IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS.* An
observed Newton order has both asserted on it. The floor — *this is at least
superlinear* — is a statement about the Jacobian and survives any precision,
because an inexact Jacobian contracts linearly whatever the arithmetic. The
ceiling — *this is a rate at all rather than a short history read as one* — is a
statement about the FIT, and an order fitted through a last residual sitting on
the floor is unbounded above: **6.15** on `XPointBorder`'s bootstrap. So the
ceiling is skipped and the floor is not, which leaves the assertion that has
teeth.

### M-224

**A BINARY DID NOT KNOW WHICH TREE IT CAME FROM, AND NEITHER DID ANYTHING IT
WROTE.** `build/meq`, linked at 13:41 from a working tree at `6a078e2`, reported
`MEQ 0.1.0 (6d4b68a)` — five commits stale — and the `machine-f-diiid.nc` it
wrote minutes later carried `:meq_version = "0.1.0 (6d4b68a)"`.

**THE MECHANISM IS A CONFIGURE-TIME `execute_process()`.** `CMakeLists.txt`
read `git rev-parse --short HEAD` while configuring the build directory and
`configure_file`d it into `meq_version.hpp`, so the commit is frozen the day
`cmake -B build` is first run and every binary that directory ever produces
carries it. Nothing re-reads it, nothing warns, and the string is
plausible — it is a real commit of this repository, merely not this one.

**IT IS A PROVENANCE DEFECT RATHER THAN A COSMETIC ONE, AND THREE THINGS IN THIS
TREE REST ON IT.** `CLAUDE.md`'s method for separating *this was already
failing* from *I broke it* is to build `HEAD` in a `git worktree` and compare
two binaries. The whole device programme is a comparison between two builds.
And `docs/running.rst` tells a user that the answer to *which equilibrium did
this plot come from* is a file that can be re-run.

**AND THE FILE SAID NOTHING ABOUT THE BUILD AT ALL, WHICH IS THE LARGER HALF.**
`meq --version` reported neither the precision nor the device backends, and
neither did any output file — so an equilibrium written by the single-precision
build and one written by the double build were **indistinguishable from their
own attributes**, while [M-204](#m-204) measures the same quantity at
`2.2 × eps` on one machine and `1,260 × eps` on another. *An accuracy qualified
per problem and per format is unreadable from a file that records neither.*

The repair is `cmake/GitCommit.cmake`, run as a build step rather than at
configure time and writing through `copy_if_different` so the relink happens
when the commit moves and not once per build, with a `-dirty` suffix from
`git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` — tracked files only, because this
repository's root holds hundreds of untracked run products and a flag that is
always set means nothing. `meq::realPrecision()` and `meq::deviceBackends()` are
the other half, in `src/meq/BuildInfo.cpp` **and not in a header**: they are
answers about MFEM's own preprocessor, and `CLAUDE.md` records
`MachineFixedBoundary.cpp` testing `#ifdef MFEM_USE_SINGLE` in a translation
unit that included no MFEM header, where the guard compiled, ran and silently
took the other branch.
