### M-226

**PHASE B EXISTED, RAN SIXTEEN TIMES INSIDE PHASE C, AND NO INSTRUMENT IN THIS
PROJECT COULD SEE IT.** `DEVICE-PLAN.md` §3.3 divides a resident solve into
*setup · one upload · device only · one download · output*, and §4 stage 4b's
acceptance — the one number this project trusts about residency — is a count of
**host reads**. Phase B is an **upload**. *An instrument that can see one
direction of the bus cannot measure a plan whose first phase is an upload*, and
stage 4b has reported a figure in the other direction and called it the
residency acceptance for as long as it has existed.

`meq::countedDeviceRead()` is the mirror of `meq::countedHostRead()` — it asks
`HostIsValid() && !DeviceIsValid()` before a `Read()`, which is exactly when a
device read moves data — and `meq::PhaseScope` attributes every crossing to the
phase it happened in. `machine-f-diiid`, `--device cuda`, 12 Newton steps over
three support sweeps, `MKL_NUM_THREADS=1`.

**AND THE HEADLINE WAS NOT A MEASUREMENT OF THE SOLVE.** Split by phase, the
published *0.2 transfers a step* is **three transfers in phase A**, divided by a
Newton step count — a rate for a phase those transfers do not occur in. Phase C,
the phase the acceptance is about, reads **zero**:

| phase | host-read funnels | transfers down | device-read funnels | uploads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** setup | 9 | **3** | 0 | 0 |
| **B** upload | 0 | 0 | 6 | **6** |
| **C** solve | 10,710 | **0** | 188 | **0** |
| **D** download | 12 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **E** output | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

**PHASE C's ZERO IS NOT RESIDENCY, AND THAT IS WHY THE TRANSFER COUNT CANNOT BE
THE ACCEPTANCE ON ITS OWN.** 10,710 host reads that move nothing means the state
is host-valid throughout, which is the *opposite* of resident. The counter reads
the same `0` for a perfectly resident solve and for one where nothing reaches the
device at all. Only the upload count beside it separates them: **residency
arriving looks like uploads in B, zero in C and one download in D; nothing on the
device looks like zero everywhere.** Today MEQ has the phase-B half of that shape
and none of the phase-D half — `0.888 MB` still comes down, and it comes down in
phase A rather than in D.

**PHASE E HAS NO FUNNELS AT ALL, WHICH IS A COVERAGE STATEMENT AND NOT A GOOD
RESULT.** The output stage reads through MFEM's own `GridFunction` accessors,
which no funnel of MEQ's can see — [M-198](#m-198)'s limit, unchanged and now
visible as an empty row rather than hidden in a total.

**AND PHASE B WAS A PROLOGUE NOWHERE: IT WAS RE-RUN ONCE PER OPERATOR REBUILD,
AND THE OPERATOR IS REBUILT PER SUPPORT SWEEP AND AFTER EVERY RIGHT-HAND-SIDE
RE-ASSEMBLY.** Five per-mesh constants — the source's knots, the coil table,
XP-1's per-element flags and the conductor cache with its offsets — were members
of `meq::DeviceNPCOperator` and were uploaded in its constructor. Moving them
into a `meq::DeviceConstants` the caller owns, and uploading only what a
comparison against host shadows says has changed:

| where phase B's buffers live | uploads | MB | `psi_ax` | constraint |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the operator, rebuilt 16× | 80 | 1.22 | 3.759851e-01 | −6.465e-12 |
| a local of `solveWithNormalisation()` | 15 | 0.228 | 3.759851e-01 | −6.465e-12 |
| a solver member, filled raw | 5 | 0.0761 | **3.759845e-01** | **−6.459e-12** |
| a solver member, `HostWrite()` first | **6** | **0.113** | 3.759851e-01 | −6.465e-12 |

**13× fewer uploads and 11× fewer bytes, with every printed digit of the host's
answer** — and the third row is the finding.

**HOISTING WORK OUT OF A LOOP CREATED A DEVICE DEFECT THE UN-HOISTED VERSION
COULD NOT HAVE HAD, AND IT IS [M-211](#m-211)'s, MET FROM THE OTHER SIDE.** The
constructor built these arrays **fresh** every time, and a fresh `mfem::Array`
has `UseDevice()` false, so filling it through `operator[]` was safe. A
persistent object fills them **in place**; `SetSize()` at an unchanged size
reallocates nothing; so the fill is a raw host write into a buffer whose live
copy is on the device, and the `Read()` after it copies nothing because MFEM
still believes the device copy is current. The plasma support changes between
sweeps, the device keeps the old flags, and the run converges to a
**neighbouring answer** — 1.6e-6 relative in `psi_ax`, with every other printed
line healthy and the bordered constraint still satisfied at 1e-12, because *a
bordered row certifies consistency and not correctness* ([M-206](#m-206)).
**`HostWrite()` before each fill is the repair**, which is `meq::DeviceRows`'
own and was already written down. *A fill that is safe in a constructor is not
safe in a refresh*, and the whole of phase B is turning the first into the
second.

**THE INSTRUMENT FOUND IT, AND NOTHING ELSE IN THE PROJECT COULD HAVE.** The
per-site table read **`2 device reads, 1 upload`** on the flag buffer — a fill
that happened and a transfer that did not, on consecutive lines of one report.
A clock cannot see a copy that did not occur; the download counter cannot see
this direction at all; `Device( "debug" )` is blind to it, because every flag was
honest about a location and wrong only about which copy was newer, which is
[M-206](#m-206)'s recorded limit. **The upload counter was built to measure
phase B and its first act was to catch a wrong answer in the change that
created it.**

**AND THE PREDICTION WAS WRONG TWICE.** Seven uploads was the arithmetic — five
constants plus two support sweeps — and the measurement read 15, then 5, then 6.
15, because a local of `solveWithNormalisation()` dies once per `solve()` and the
support sweeps rebuild it: *a buffer whose lifetime is a solve cannot be uploaded
once per mesh, however carefully it is refreshed.* 5, because the missed fill
suppressed the re-upload the support change should have caused — the wrong
number and the wrong answer were **the same defect**, and the one that looked
better was the broken one. 6 is five constants up once and the flags up again
when the support genuinely moves, which is what the plan asks for.

**A MEMBER IS SAFE ACROSS AN ADAPTIVE MESH CHANGE BY CONSTRUCTION RATHER THAN BY
DISCIPLINE, WHICH IS WHY THERE IS NO INVALIDATION HOOK.** `refresh()` decides
what to upload by comparing against host shadows, and a refined mesh changes the
element count — so the flags, the shift offsets and the conductor cache differ in
size and re-upload, while the source's knots and coils correctly do not. *A flag
somebody has to remember to clear is the thing this avoids.*

**PHASE D NOW EXISTS AND IS FREE, WHICH IS THE SAME SENTENCE TWICE.**
`downloadSolution()` funnels `solution` and its three long-lived aliases — all
four, because an alias carries its own validity flags and a read of the base
cannot see data still on an alias ([M-79](#m-79)) — and it moves **nothing**,
because the host trace solve and `NPCRecover` have already left the state on the
host. That is phase D costing zero for exactly the reason residency has not
arrived: there is nothing to bring back. It is built now so that the number is
read where the answer returns rather than wherever a reader happens to touch it
first.

### M-227

**THE BORDERED COLUMNS ARE NOT BROUGHT DOWN BY THE FLUSH — THEY ARE NEVER ON
THE DEVICE AT ALL, AND THAT MOVES ITEM 4's GATE BEHIND ITEM 6.**
`DEVICE-PLAN.md` §3.3 item 4 gates `meq::DeviceRows::dotAll()` on
`Memory::DeviceIsValid()` of the solved columns, and both the plan and the code
beside it say `flush()` *"deliberately brings every solved column to the
HOST"* — which reads as though the host-side dense elimination is what holds
the gate shut, and is how this project's own ordered list described it.

`meq::stageChecksum()` reports a buffer's **validity flags before it reads**,
which is the half a plain checksum lacks. Probed at the first statement after
`npcLinear.ArrayMult()`, ahead of the funnel, on `machine-f-diiid` under
`--device cuda`, `MKL_NUM_THREADS=1`:

| border columns probed over a 12-step run | flags | count |
|---|---|---|
| `border.column`, n = 109,203 each | **`H+ D-`** | **168 of 168** |

**Host-valid and device-INVALID, every one.** Not *brought* down — never up.
The funnel below the probe therefore moves nothing, which the crossing counter
independently confirms: that site reports **0 transfers** against the whole
run's 3 ([M-226](#m-226)).

**SO THE DENSE ELIMINATION IS NOT THE BLOCKER, AND NAMING IT WAS A GUESS
DRESSED AS A DIAGNOSIS.** The bordered Schur complement is `( N + 4 )²`
scalars — order 14 on this case — and the two operations that touch the
full-size columns after it are `mfem::Vector::Add()` and `Norml2()`, **both
device-aware already**: `Add()` is `ReadWrite()` plus a `forall`, and
[M-195](#m-195) recorded `Norml2()` as an `mfem::reduce`. Porting the dense
solve would move arithmetic that is already free and change nothing about where
the columns live.

**THE PRODUCER IS WHAT DECIDES, AND THE PRODUCER IS PARDISO.**
`CanBatchNPCTraversal()` reads **yes** here — `NPCReduce` and `NPCRecover` are
both kernels ([M-212](#m-212)) — and the output is still host-only, because the
trace solve sandwiched between them is a **host** direct solver. A batched
traversal around a host solve produces a host answer. *A leg's residency is a
property of what produces its data, not of what consumes it.*

**WHICH PUTS ITEM 4 STRICTLY AFTER ITEM 6 AND CONFIRMS §3.3's ORDERING FOR A
REASON §3.3 DID NOT GIVE.** The plan orders cuDSS last to protect the
digit-for-digit instrument — a choice about what can be *validated*. This is a
second and independent reason: until the trace solve is on the device there is
no device-resident column for `dotAll()` to read, so item 4 cannot turn on
whatever is done to the dense arithmetic. **And pushing them up instead is
already measured as a loss** — [M-208](#m-208)'s 33.1 transfers and 55.1 MB
against 3 and 0.888 MB, an 11× and 62× cost, because *no amount of kernel makes
an h2d of the state cheaper than a gather from it.*

**THE INSTRUMENT WAS THE ONE ALREADY IN THE TREE AND IT TOOK ONE PROBE.**
`meq::StageChecksum` exists because [M-206](#m-206) needed it and it was kept
that time; the question *"where is this buffer actually"* had simply never been
asked at this site, and the comment that stood there answered it by assertion.
*A comment describing a mechanism is a hypothesis until something reads the
flags.* Same species as `ComputeHDGFaceEnergy()`'s line-range error and the
`darcyform.hpp` doxygen that this project carried as its largest dependency for
months — and the cost here was a plan item ordered against a cause that was not
the cause.

### M-228

**`DeviceParity` GAINS A REAL-CUDA ARM, AND THE REASON IT DID NOT HAVE ONE WAS
BACKWARDS.** The case ran `--device cpu` against `--device debug` and
`DEVICE-PLAN.md` §4 stage 0 named the missing CUDA coverage *"a gap worth naming
rather than closing with a second slow case"*. **`debug` is the slow arm.** It
has device memory semantics with host arithmetic and `mprotect`s the host page,
so it pays for every protection fault; a card run does the same work on the
card.

| `machine-f-diiid`, `mhd-rectangle` | seconds |
|---|---|
| `DeviceParity` before, cpu + debug | 392 |
| `DeviceParity` after, cpu + debug + cuda | **427** |

**35 seconds for the arm that covers the class the other two cannot.**

| case | arm | Newton | `psi_ax` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `machine-f-diiid` | cpu · debug · **cuda** | 2 · 2 · **2** | 3.759851e-01 · 3.759851e-01 · **3.759851e-01** |
| `mhd-rectangle` | cpu · debug · **cuda** | 5 · 5 · **5** | — (no border) |

**AND IT IS NOT A REPEAT OF THE `debug` ARM, WHICH IS THE WHOLE JUSTIFICATION.**
The file's own header claimed the iteration-count assertion was what the
stale-copy class needed. **That is M-187's class** — an answer right to every
digit on four times the work. **[M-206](#m-206) defeats both instruments at
once**: a 43-solve outer loop ran to completion under `debug` **without faulting
once**, `psi_ax` came back wrong by a **factor of two**, and the inner bordered
solve took the **same four Newton steps** on both arms. `debug` protects a page
and so catches a raw read of the **wrong location**; it is blind to honest flags
over a **stale copy**, and no count can see a value that is merely old. What
found M-206 was `cpu` against `cuda`, stage by stage. *A green `debug` arm is
not evidence about the card.*

**THE SKIP IS READ OFF MFEM'S OWN OUTPUT AND NOT INFERRED FROM AN EXIT CODE.**
A build carrying CUDA on a machine with no card and a device that disagrees
share an exit status, so the arm asks whether MFEM printed
`Device configuration: cuda` and treats its absence as an absence. *An absent
GPU is not a disagreement*, and a test that cannot tell the two apart either
fails everywhere or skips silently — the second being worse than having no test,
which is why the skipped row prints its reason.

**AND IT HAD TO BE ADDED BEFORE ITEM 6, NOT AFTER.** §3.5 records that cuDSS as
the device default ends *"`--device cuda` reproduces `--device cpu` to every
printed digit"* — 0.8.0 is nondeterministic run to run at up to 3.6e-15 with no
usable switch at `N + 4` right-hand sides. So every digit-for-digit arm must be
pinned **while the trace solve is still PARDISO**; afterwards the same assertion
can only be written as a tolerance. *The cheapest moment to buy an exact
instrument is the last one before it stops being available.*

**THE COMPILE-TIME HALF IS LEGITIMATE HERE AND IS NOT ALWAYS.**
`#ifdef MFEM_USE_CUDA` decides whether to try, and this translation unit
includes `mfem.hpp` — which is what makes the test mean anything.
`MachineFixedBoundary.cpp` drives the shipped binary, needs nothing of the
library, included no MFEM header, and its `#ifdef MFEM_USE_SINGLE` compiled, ran
and silently took the other branch, because a configuration macro in a TU that
has not included MFEM is not false but **undefined**.

### M-229

**cuDSS IS THE TRACE SOLVER UNDER CUDA, AND IT TURNS OUT TO BE NECESSARY AND
NOWHERE NEAR SUFFICIENT.** `DEVICE-PLAN.md` §3.3 item 6, taken deliberately and
with the exact baseline banked first ([M-228](#m-228)). The driver now defaults
to cuDSS when `Backend::CUDA_MASK` is allowed and the file named no trace
solver.

**`CUDA_MASK` AND NOT `DEVICE_MASK`, WHICH IS NOT A DETAIL.**
`DEVICE_MASK = CUDA_MASK | HIP_MASK | DEBUG_DEVICE`, so `--device debug` is a
Device by that test — and it is a Device with no GPU execution in the process,
where a CUDA library has nothing to run on. The two batched keys beside it are
right to use `DEVICE_MASK` because they are about memory and routes; this one is
about a vendor library actually executing.

**THE NONDETERMINISM IS REAL AND IS BELOW THE PRINTED PRECISION, WHICH §3.5 DID
NOT PREDICT.** Three runs of `machine-f-diiid` report the bordered constraint at
`-6.465e-12`, `-6.466e-12`, `-6.466e-12` where PARDISO is stable — so cuDSS is
live and is varying at about 1e-15 absolute, as 0.8.0's open
`CUDSS_CONFIG_DETERMINISTIC_MODE` implies. But over **eight** repeat runs every
field `DeviceParity` compares is **identical**:

| eight `--device cuda` runs | value | distinct |
|---|---|---|
| Newton steps | 2 | **1 of 8** |
| `psi_ax` | 3.759851e-01 | **1 of 8** |
| `psi_bnd` | 7.081394e-02 | **1 of 8** |
| X-point | ( 1.200929, −0.999491 ) | **1 of 8** |

**So the exact assertion stays exact, and what it now rests on has changed.** It
was resting on determinism; it rests on the driver printing seven significant
figures of a quantity perturbed at the fifteenth. *That is a weaker foundation
and it is still a true one*, so the repair is to say so rather than to pre-emptively
widen a tolerance — and if it ever flickers, the tolerance to use is the measured
spread above and not a convenient one.

**WHAT ITEM 6 WAS SUPPOSED TO BUY WAS RESIDENCY, AND IT DID NOT BUY IT.**
[M-227](#m-227) found the bordered columns `H+ D-` at the flush and named the
host trace solve as the cause. With cuDSS in they were still **168 of 168
`H+ D-`** — because the columns are declared `mfem::Vector v( n )`, and **a
freshly constructed `mfem::Vector` has `UseDevice()` false**, so `Write()` hands
back a host pointer and every kernel filling one fills host memory. *Item 4's
gate was a predicate on data that could not satisfy it under any trace solver,
and it reported the same NO for both reasons.*

**MAKING THEM DEVICE-CAPABLE WORKED, AND MADE THE RUN SEVENTEEN TIMES WORSE.**
`UseDevice( true )` on the five output families — `y`, `z`, `zL`, `zB`,
`exteriorZ` — plus skipping the flush funnel where the device route is eligible:

| | columns device-valid at the flush | transfers | MB | `psi_ax` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PARDISO | 0 of 168 | 3 | 0.888 | 3.759851e-01 |
| cuDSS | 0 of 168 | 3 | 0.888 | 3.759851e-01 |
| cuDSS + `UseDevice( true )` | **126 of 168** | **20** | **15.1** | 3.759851e-01 |

**THE CROSSING DID NOT DISAPPEAR — IT MOVED, AND THE SITE IT MOVED TO IS THE
FINDING.** 15 of the 20 transfers land on one line: the **axis constraint's**
read of the iterate, 12.5 MB. The trial step is
`unknown.Add( -damping, y )`, so a device-valid column makes the **iterate**
device-valid, and the next step's axis constraint — a host mesh search — drags
the whole state back. That is §3.3's *alternation*, previously an argument and
now a counted 1.4 transfers a step.

**SO RESIDENCY IS A PROPERTY OF A CYCLE AND NOT OF A LEG, AND NO PER-ITEM
ORDERING CAN EXPRESS THAT.** Every leg of a Newton step must be device-side
**together**, or the one host leg pulls the state down and converts every other
leg's kernel into an upload. The trace solve is now cuDSS, the NPC traversal and
the integrand are kernels, and the row dots and `I_p` are **built** — and
`meq::plasmaCurrentPerElementOnDevice()` has **no caller at all**, deferred in
M-192 for the same reason `dotAll()` was in M-208: *a device reduction is
correct as soon as it is written and only pays once the state is already
resident.* **Every leg was waiting for the state to be resident, and the state
can only be resident if they all move at once.**

**AND THE LAST ONE IS A MESH SEARCH, WHICH §3.4 ALREADY CALLED THE HARDEST PART
OF THE PAGE.** The axis constraint roots the solved `q`; its sibling the limiter
was measured **not worth porting** ([M-201](#m-201)). So the cycle cannot be
closed by wiring what is already built, and the `UseDevice( true )` arm is
reverted — kept as a measurement rather than as code, because shipping it is a
17× regression in bus traffic by the one metric this machine can honour.

**WHAT IS KEPT IS cuDSS AND THE PREPARED FUNNEL.** `flush()` now skips its host
funnel when the device route is eligible — decided **before** the flush, since
asking `DeviceIsValid()` after it is a cycle rather than a measurement — and a
failed device route is still safe, because `CompressedRows::gather()` opens with
`v.HostRead()` and funnels for itself.

### M-230

**A `MFEM_HOST_DEVICE` BASIS ON THE REFERENCE TRIANGLE, WHICH TWO PLACES IN
THE TREE HAD ALREADY NAMED AS THE BLOCKER.**
`src/meq/PointLocatorDevice.cpp` opens by saying what it cannot do — *"IT
LOCATES, IT DOES NOT INTERPOLATE. Evaluating the field needs
`FiniteElement::CalcShape`, which is a host virtual taking an
`mfem::IntegrationPoint`. A device evaluation needs a `MFEM_HOST_DEVICE` basis
and that is `DEVICE-PLAN.md` item 3's blocker"* — and §3.4 calls the axis
constraint the hardest item on the page. **They are one blocker seen from two
sides**, and `meq::DeviceBasis` is it.

**A FIXED QUADRATURE RULE IS NOT THE ANSWER, WHICH IS WHY THIS HAD TO EXIST.**
`FiniteElement::GetDofToQuad()` already hands shape functions to a device, and
`meq::plasmaCurrentPerElementOnDevice()` needs nothing more — but it supplies
`phi_i` at the points of ONE `mfem::IntegrationRule`, decided before the
launch. That is everything an INTEGRAL needs and nothing a SEARCH needs:
`rootInElement()` evaluates wherever its iterate has got to and is documented
to let it leave the element by two reference units. *A rule is a set of points;
a search needs a function.*

**THE CONSTRUCTION BORROWS NOTHING FROM MFEM'S INTERNALS.** The host asks the
element for its own shape functions at its own nodes and solves for the
constant matrix re-expressing them in barycentric monomials:
`M( a, b ) = B_b( node_a )`, `S( a, i ) = phi_i( node_a )`, `T = M^-1 S`, with
the Bernstein multinomial folded into `T`'s rows so the kernel evaluates plain
powers. `T` depends on the geometry, the degree and the basis type and on
nothing about the solution, so it is §3.3's **phase B in its purest form**.

| degree | cond( M ) | reconstruction, containment band | **absolute**, abandon bound | value vs `GetValue` | gradient vs `GetGradient` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.0 | 1.9e-16 | 4.4e-16 | 1.1e-16 | 0 exactly |
| 2 | 3.0 | 6.9e-16 | 1.6e-14 | 2.2e-16 | 4.3e-16 |
| 3 | 11.0 | 8.3e-16 | 6.3e-13 | 5.0e-16 | 9.6e-16 |
| 4 | 22.6 | 5.3e-15 | **1.27e-11** | 8.7e-16 | 4.2e-15 |

(relative except where marked; `tests/unit/DeviceBasisTests.cpp` prints all of
it every run, and the probe points include several well OUTSIDE the element.)

**THE CEILING IS A MEASURED CONDITIONING BOUND AND NOT AN ARRAY SIZE, WHICH IS
THE CORRECTION WORTH KEEPING.** The first draft set it at six, on the sound
argument that the limit is the per-thread coefficient array and a kernel that
spills is slow rather than wrong. **That is true inside the element and false
outside it**, which is where this evaluator's caller spends part of its Newton:
the absolute disagreement at the abandon bound grows by about **twenty per
degree**, and taken with the ceiling temporarily at six, degrees 5 and 6 read
**1.6e-09 and 4.8e-07**. At 4.8e-07 a stopping target of `1e-13 max | q |` is
unreachable, and a search whose residual cannot fall below its target runs to
its cap and reports nothing. `lambda0` goes negative out there and `lambda0^p`
carries the growth, where MFEM's own recursion degrades far more slowly. **So
the ceiling is 4, every degree accepted is swept by the test, and raising it
means a better conditioned device basis rather than a larger array.**

**AND THE AFFINE MAP IS MFEM'S OWN, ASKED RATHER THAN REPRODUCED FROM THE
VERTICES.** `ElementTransformation::Jacobian()` is **bitwise constant** over a
straight-sided triangle — measured, exactly 0 difference at three well-separated
reference points — and `Transform` agrees with `v0 + J ( xi, eta )` to one ulp.
Affineness is then measured per element by comparing the Jacobian at two points
rather than inferred from `Mesh::GetNodes() == nullptr`, because CLAUDE.md
records a mesh ACQUIRING nodes without becoming curved and `meq::GridSampler`
paying two orders of magnitude for reading that pointer as the question.

### M-231

**THE AXIS CONSTRAINT'S MESH SEARCH, ON THE DEVICE — AND THE ACCEPTANCE IS THE
CANDIDATE LIST RATHER THAN THE ANSWER.**
`meq::axisCandidatesOnDevice()` roots every element with one thread each,
porting `rootInElement()` and the `referenceJacobian()` it calls line for line:
same seeds, same central-difference step with the same stencil sliding, same
Cramer solve, same unit step truncation, same two-diameter abandon, same
`containment + 1e-9` acceptance, same degeneracy threshold, same classification
ladder. The iteration is in REFERENCE coordinates throughout, which is what
makes the port exact where it matters.

| degree | host `sweep()` candidates | device, merged | before the merge | device → host | host → device | `psi` at a matched point |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5 | 5 | 20 | 4.5e-14 | 4.5e-14 | |
| 2 | 5 | 5 | 28 | 2.2e-16 | 2.2e-16 | 7.8e-16 |
| 3 | 5 | 5 | 28 | 6.5e-16 | 6.5e-16 | |

Both directions, because a one-sided check misses half: a kernel finding a
SUBSET passes *every device point is a host point*, and one accepting spurious
roots passes the converse. The stopping scale agrees **exactly** — a max is
exactly associative and `( -a )*( -a )` is `a*a`, so unlike everything else
here that one is a `==`.

**THE MERGE IS THE HOST'S AND SKIPPING IT CHANGES ANSWERS, WHICH THE FIRST
VERSION GOT WRONG ON A TRUE ARGUMENT.** The device list was first left
unmerged, on the reasoning that both selection rules — largest score, nearest
the previous axis — are invariant under duplicates. That reasoning is correct
and it is about the wrong thing: `sweep()` does not merely drop exact
duplicates, it merges two candidates of the same type within **half an
element**, keeping the one least outside its own. Those are not copies but one
critical point rooted from two neighbouring elements' polynomials, landing in
two places with two values of `psi` — measured **7.2e-03, 4.3e-03 and 7.5e-04**
apart at `k = 1, 2, 3`, which is interpolation error and not round-off. *Two
representations of one critical point are not duplicates.*
`CriticalPointFinder::mergeCandidates()` is now public and both routes call it.

**AND `DeviceParity` COULD NOT HAVE FOUND THAT.** `machine-f-diiid` reports
`psi_ax = 3.759851e-01` to every printed digit with the merge in or out,
because there the right candidate wins both competitions. *A test on the final
answer passes a port that found a different set and picked the same one.*

**A SEMANTIC DIFFERENCE IS KEPT AND STATED.** The host's warm path stops at the
first ring holding a clean root; the device roots every element — on a card
4,848 Newtons and 19 Newtons are one launch, so M-100's 40× economy inverts —
and the host then picks the nearest clean root GLOBALLY. They agree whenever
the nearest clean root lies in that first productive ring, which is the case
the ring walk exists for.

**AND IT FOUND A DORMANT DEFECT OF MEQ'S OWN, BY REMOVING A FUNNEL.**
`mfem::Device( "debug" )` aborted on the first run: `coldState( unknown )` is a
copy construction whose SOURCE is funnelled — M-205's repair — while the
DESTINATION is not. `Vector::Vector( Vector const & )` propagates `UseDevice()`
and copies device-to-device, so `coldState` is born device-valid with its host
page protected, and the three raw loops after it write 698,112 bytes into it.
***Funnelling the source of a copy does not funnel the copy.*** It was
unreachable until the axis constraint stopped downloading the iterate, because
that funnel ran first on every path — M-130's *ordering has protected it so
far* for the third time, and **the first time DELETING a funnel is what exposed
the next one.**

### M-232

**THE SAME 12.5 MB MOVED THREE TIMES, AND THAT IS THE MEASUREMENT.**
With the device routes forced open on `machine-f-diiid` under `--device cuda`:

| | transfers | MB | largest site | `psi_ax` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| committed | 3 | 0.888 | — (phase A) | 3.759851e-01 |
| axis search on the device | 53 | 15.9 | **`refreshXPoint()`, 15 × 830 KB** | 3.759851e-01 |
| + the X-point evaluation | 69 | 15.9 | **`limiterValue()`, 15 × 830 KB** | 3.759851e-01 |
| gated on residency | **3** | **0.888** | — | 3.759851e-01 |

The axis constraint's own 12.5 MB duly disappears each time — and the identical
12.5 MB reappears at the next host leg, which had been reading a copy the first
one paid for. **The iterate was crossing the bus ONCE A STEP and every host leg
after the first rode on it for nothing.**

**SO A LEG PORTED IN ISOLATION DOES NOT REMOVE A TRANSFER, IT RENAMES ONE**,
and the count falls only when the LAST host reader of the iterate goes. That is
[M-229](#m-229)'s *residency is a property of a cycle and not of a leg*,
demonstrated from the other direction and three times over rather than argued
once. **A per-site table attributes a transfer to whoever asks first, which is
not the same as attributing it to whoever needs it** — and the committed
headline of 3 transfers was never a measurement of how little the iterate
moves, only of how little it moved while nothing had put it on the device.

**THE GATE IS A PREDICATE ABOUT THE DATA**, `DeviceIsValid() && !HostIsValid()`
— the same shape `columnIsResident()` has for `meq::DeviceRows` and for the
same reason: it is the only form that is right both before and after residency
arrives. `H- D+` is the one state in which the device route is the cheaper one;
with the host holding a live copy there is nothing to buy, and with the host
holding the ONLY live copy the device route pays an upload to avoid a download
that would not have happened. Both routes are therefore **inert today and
switch on with no further edit**, which is the arrangement `meq::DeviceRows`
has been in since M-208 and `meq::plasmaCurrentPerElementOnDevice()` since
M-192.

**WHAT IS LEFT IS A COUNT AND NOT A DIFFICULTY.** Ten host legs still read the
iterate — the limiter contact, the plasma current and its two columns, the
transmission constraint, the nodal-maximum fallback and the rest — and every
one of them is a reduction or a point evaluation of the kind
`meq::DeviceBasis` and `meq::DeviceQuadrature` now both serve. None is a search;
the search was the hard one and it is done.

### M-233

**THE AXIS KERNEL WAS 65x OFF ITS OWN ARITHMETIC, AND TWO THIRDS OF THAT WAS
TWO SERIAL SCANS AND A RUNTIME LOOP BOUND.**

`meq::axisCandidatesOnDevice()` as first written took **297 ms** to root
102,840 elements -- 2.9 us an element, against the ~4.5 ms the flop count and
this card's FP64 rate give. Three causes, found with `-Xptxas -v` and a thread
count rather than guessed:

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **the two reductions were `mfem::forall( 1, ... )`** | the flux scale walked **1.23 million dofs on one CUDA core** and the compaction 205,680 slots | the comment justified it as *"thirty microseconds of serial walk"* -- an estimate made against a case forty times smaller, and wrong by that factor |
| **a runtime loop bound** | `basis.dofs` is not a constant, so nvcc could not unroll; `coefficients[ at ]` stayed a dynamic index and the three per-thread arrays went to LOCAL MEMORY -- **608 bytes of stack frame with ZERO register spills**, which is what that pairing means | at 1024 threads an SM carries 622 KB of local working set against 64 KB of L1 |
| **the cap was a download budget** | the compacted array came back WHOLE, so 256 was the most it could hold | one refusal on `fixed-f-diiid` cost a **22.4 second** host sweep |

| `fixed-f-diiid`, 102,840 elements, per device sweep | |
|---|---|
| as first written | **297 ms** |
| + two-stage max and order-preserving stream compaction | 89 ms |
| + the degree as a template parameter | **11.9 ms** |

**25x, and the answer did not move**: the candidate lists are bit-identical to
the single-threaded version's at every degree, and the stopping scale still
reads `0.0 eps` apart from `fluxScale()`'s own. 116 ns an element is about
2.6x off this card's FP64 peak for the flop count.

**THE SECOND ROW IS THE ONE WORTH KEEPING.** Halving
`meq::triangleBasisMaxDegree` as a diagnostic took the stack frame from 608 to
**272** bytes, accounting for the array sizes exactly -- which is what said the
arrays were the whole of it, before any refactor. Templating on the degree then
took it to **0 bytes and 96 registers**. *A stack frame with no spills is not a
register-pressure problem; it is an array the compiler could not see the bounds
of.*

**AND IT IS NOT `mfem::reduce`, WHICH IS THE ONE PLACE THE STANDING PREFERENCE
FOR MFEM'S ABSTRACTIONS GIVES WAY.** That routine takes `T &res`, a HOST
reference, so the one scalar these kernels keep on the device would come back
and be pushed out again -- a download and an upload per constraint evaluation
of the number `meq::AxisSearchInputs::target` points at. The two-stage form
keeps it where it is, and `fmax` being associative AND commutative means
nothing is given up for it; `meq::DeviceRows` refuses the same primitive for
the opposite reason, its sum having an order to reproduce.

**WHAT IS LEFT IS NOT THE KERNEL.** The leg is now one declined call: at a
near-zero iterate `max | q |` collapses, the stopping rule becomes absolute,
every element reports a root at its own seed and the list is `2 x elements`
long. The route refuses it -- and **the host meets the same pathology**,
paying 22.4 s for that one sweep and eleven of them over a `--device cpu` run.
*That is a property of the stopping rule on a degenerate iterate, not of
either route.*

### M-234

**THE SEARCH IS OVER A NEIGHBOURHOOD AND THE INDEX FOR IT WAS ALREADY IN THE
TREE.**

[M-231](#m-231)'s port swept every element on every call, which is 36x the
host's warm ring search per call on `machine-f-diiid` and 7.1x FASTER than its
cold sweep on `fixed-f-diiid` -- a win exactly when the seed keeps failing and
a loss when it works. The answer is the one the host already takes and the
device can afford better: root a BLOCK around the previous axis, and let the
block be generous because a thousand elements costs about what one launch does.

**AND "FINDING THOSE CELLS" IS NOT THE PAIN POINT, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON
THIS IS CHEAP.** `meq::PointLocator` builds a uniform bin grid over element
bounding boxes in CSR form -- about one element per bin, geometry only,
therefore phase B -- for a completely different purpose, the warm start's point
location. A spatial neighbourhood is a block of its bins and is O( 1 ) to name.
`PointLocator::grid()` exposes it so there is ONE grid rather than two uploads
of one table.

| `machine-f-diiid`, the axis leg per call | |
|---|---|
| host, `--device cpu`, 8 threads | 1.6 ms wall at **7.01 cores** |
| device, sweeping every element ([M-233](#m-233)) | 3.0 ms |
| device, neighbourhood of 1024 | **1.7 ms at 1.00 core** |

**Parity with seven host cores on one**, and `psi_ax` unmoved. On
`fixed-f-diiid`'s 102,840 elements a neighbourhood call is about 13 ms against
a full device sweep's 11.9 and a threaded host sweep's 2,121.

**THE WIDENING IS WHAT MAKES A BOUNDED SEARCH SAFE AND IT IS NOT DECORATION.**
A neighbourhood that silently missed the axis would hand the selection a
competition its winner was not entered in, and the selection cannot tell that
from there being no axis at all. So a warm attempt that finds nothing is
retried over the whole mesh before the route gives up -- the ring walk's own
structure, widen then give up, with the widening in one step. On
`fixed-f-diiid` from a cold start it fires about half the time, because the
axis moves further in the first Newton steps than any fixed block covers; on
the warm-started machine case it never fires.

**WHAT IS LEFT IS NOT THE SEARCH AND IT BELONGS TO BOTH ROUTES.** The first
evaluation of a `fixed-f-diiid` run costs **21 s** whoever makes it. At a
near-zero iterate `max | q |` collapses, `fluxScale()` falls back to 1.0, and
the stopping rule becomes `residual <= tolerance` in ABSOLUTE terms -- which
every element meets at its own seed, so every element reports a root and the
list is `2 x elements` long. Letting the device take it (cap raised to a
million, the download already being proportional to the count) removes the host
sweep entirely -- **0 cold sweeps, 24 taken, 0 declined** -- and moves the leg
only 21.4 s to 19.6 s, because the cost follows the list to whoever handles it.
*That is the stopping rule on a degenerate iterate and not a property of either
route*, and the cap is left at 4096 because a refusal and an acceptance cost
the same there while the refusal bounds the bus.

### M-235

WAS SUPPOSED TO SETTLE THE DEVICE QUESTION WAS MEASURING A BISECTION THAT COULD

Four cases, six arms, interleaved within each round in [M-135](#m-135)'s shape,

rounds (2 at `ff3`). `mf` is `machine-f-diiid`; `ff1`/`ff2`/`ff3` are

| | | 10 | sgl cuda | 259.7 | 135.5 | 97.6 | 9.758 | 2.897817e-01 |

**THE NEWTON COUNTS DIFFER BETWEEN THE FORMATS, SO A WALL COMPARISON IS
CONFOUNDED AND `solve/N` IS THE COMPARABLE COLUMN** -- `mf` takes one step in
single against two in double, `ff1` eight against ten. `psi_ax` agrees across
formats at FP32's own floor, 2.9e-06 on `mf` and 7e-07 on the `ff` family, which
is [M-184](#m-184)'s figure on four more cases. **`ff3` marks 102,836 elements
in single against 102,840** -- four elements, the level-set marking decided at
round-off, and `meq::markingOffset()`'s subject.

**THE DEVICE WINS THE PRODUCTION BORDERED CASE IN BOTH FORMATS AND LOSES THE
BIG FIXED ONES**, 0.81x and 0.85x on `mf`'s solve against 1.03x and 1.35x at
`ff3`. The fastest solve of all sixteen arms is **single + CUDA on `mf` at
2.445 s** against the double host's 3.727, 0.66x.

**AND THE REASON `ff3` LOSES IS NOT THE FP64 RATE. IT IS THAT THE PORTED AXIS
SEARCH IS NEVER ENTERED AND THE HOST FALLBACK LOSES ITS THREADING.** Both CUDA
arms print `axis and X-point field evaluations on device: 0 taken, 15 declined`
-- the gate is `DeviceIsValid() && !HostIsValid()` and is inert by design, which
is [M-232](#m-232)'s whole argument. So a device run takes the host sweep with
`meq::hostLoopsAreSafe()` false ([M-188](#m-188)):

| `ff3` axis leg | cpu8 | cuda |
|---|---|---|
| double | 21.57 s at **1.97 cores** | 33.57 s at **1.00 cores** |
| single | 24.19 s at **2.61 cores** | 51.46 s at **1.00 cores** |

That is **18.1% of the double device wall and 19.8% of the single** -- the
largest single item in a device run, 1.56x and 2.13x worse than the host's,
while [M-233](#m-233)'s 11.9 ms kernel sits beside it built, bit-identical and
idle. *The leg the port was written for is the one the device is losing on, and
it is losing on it because the port is correctly switched off.*

**SINGLE PRECISION READ AS A 1.1x TO 2.4x LOSS AND THE ARITHMETIC WAS NEVER THE
REASON.** Per call every threaded solve leg is FASTER in single, as FP32 should
be -- `ff1` residual 14.7 ms/call in double against 12.9, gradient 24.0 against
20.3, trace factorisation 47.6 against 41.5, backsolve 13.3 against 9.6. The
loss is two SINGLE-THREADED host legs: `setup` at 1.00 cores, 18.7 s against
40.2, and `re-assembly` -- one call, 1.0 cores -- 3.04 s against 8.55. Same
mesh, same 6245 elements, same 0 transfer paths widened, same 98% of the
boundary reaching `Gamma`. **Identical work, 2.15x the time.**

**THE SUSPECT WAS THE EXTENSION QUADRATURE AND IT WAS WRONG.** `meq::
extensionFdStep()` is 5.0e-3 in single against 1.0e-6 in double, a 5000x step
against a degeneracy floor that follows `eps`, and M-183 is exactly that pairing
going wrong once already -- so it was the obvious candidate and it is not the
answer. **`perf` was**, and it named `meq::BoundaryShape::shiftedAngle` at
48.1% of the double run and **68.7%** of the single. That function takes a
`double` and is in MEQ's MFEM-free half, so its arithmetic is IDENTICAL in the
two builds; its self time went 1.878 s to 5.621 s, **2.99x**, which for identical
per-call work IS the call count.

**AND TWO CONSUMERS OF THE SAME `levelSet()` SEPARATE THE CAUSE OUTRIGHT**,
which is what makes this a diagnosis rather than a profile:

| inclusive frame | double | single | absolute |
|---|---|---|---|
| `VertexConePath` -> `VertexDirection` -> `FirstCrossing` | 32.61% | **50.72%** | 4.92 s -> **15.33 s**, 3.1x |
| `MarkLevelSetSubdomain` | 10.66% | 6.63% | 1.61 s -> 2.00 s, 1.25x |

`MarkLevelSetSubdomain` calls `levelSet()` once per lattice point -- a FIXED
count -- and is flat. `FirstCrossing` is a root find whose count a tolerance
decides, and it triples. *A fixed-count consumer and a tolerance-driven consumer
of one function is a controlled experiment with the arithmetic held equal.*

**`mfem::VertexConePath`'s DEFAULT `tol_` IS `1e-13` AND A FLOAT BISECTION
CANNOT REACH IT.** `FirstCrossing()` brackets the crossing to
`length/search_steps` and halves while `tb - ta > tol*length`. In double that is
39 halvings. In single `tb - ta` floors at `eps*length`, about `1.19e-07*length`
-- **six orders ABOVE the target** -- so the condition never goes false and the
loop runs to `max_iter = 100`, on every ray of every vertex of `Gamma_h`.

**IT IS THE SEVENTH CONSTANT OF [M-184](#m-184)'S SPECIES AND THE FIRST THAT
COSTS ONLY TIME.** The other six were wrong answers -- an empty quadrature
reporting success, a `build()` refusing everything, a correct answer refused.
This one misreports nothing: the crossing IS located, to `eps`, which is better
than the target asks for and the best single can do. **So no assertion in the
tree can see it and only a clock can**, which is why a suite at
[M-222](#m-222)'s 62-of-63 parity carried it. And it is MFEM's default argument
rather than MEQ's literal, which makes it M-222's `TransformBack` finding a
second time: *the largest single item was one line of somebody else's header.*

**AND THE REPAIR IS NOT A TOLERANCE AT ALL -- IT IS THE BISECTION'S
TERMINATION, AND IT IS UPSTREAM'S.** MEQ built `meq::pathTolerance()` first,
`std::max( 1.0e-13, N eps )` at all ten construction sites, and swept `N`
against the suite. **Every value that is loose enough to help is loose enough
to move an answer**, which is the finding and is the opposite of what the first
version of this entry claimed:

| | `1e-13` (upstream) | `64 eps` | `4 eps` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ConductorSubtraction` | GREEN | **RED** | GREEN |
| `DriverAcceptance` | GREEN | RED | **RED** |
| `MachineFixedBoundary` | GREEN | GREEN | **RED** |

`DriverAcceptance` is the one that cannot be argued with: *"the driver wrote 620
elements where the same loop by hand ends at 612"*, a deterministic element
count rather than a convergence coin toss. **This constant decides where the
transfer path ENDS and the exterior datum is assembled there, so it is a
tolerance on the ANSWER**; trading its last digits for iterations buys a clock
and sells a result. MEQ's arm is reverted whole and the call sites are back on
the default.

**THE REAL FIX COSTS NO ACCURACY AND IS ONE LINE OF `FirstCrossing()`.** That
loop is a bisection, and a bisection in a finite format should stop when the
midpoint stops moving, not at an absolute bracket. Simulated in both formats
from `length/32`:

| float | iterations | error |
|---|---|---|
| `tol = 1e-13` (upstream today) | **100**, the cap | 2.980e-08 |
| `tol = 4.77e-07` (MEQ's abandoned arm) | 16 | **1.490e-07** |
| `if ( tm <= ta \|\| tm >= tb ) break;` | **20** | **2.980e-08** |

**Full accuracy in a fifth of the work**, and in DOUBLE the `1e-13` target still
fires first -- 39 halvings against the no-progress rule's 49 -- so **the double
path is bit-identical and no caller sees a change**. *The question was never
how tight to ask for; it was that the loop had no idea when it had finished.*
Reported as `HDG-PATH-BISECTION-TERMINATION-FROM-MEQ.md`.

**AND THE DEFAULT IS BEING PROPAGATED, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS WORTH A REPORT
RATHER THAN A WORKAROUND.** `tol_ = 1e-13, max_iter_ = 100` stands at
`LevelSetPath`, `VertexConePath` and the `TiltedPath` added by the 2026-10-01
path merge -- **three classes and not the four MEQ reported**, since
`ClosestPointPath` is a closed form with no bisection in it. All three reach the
one `FirstCrossing()`, so one line covers every caller. A consumer in single
precision meets the pair at each of them.

**THE FIX IS LANDED, TAKEN AS WRITTEN, AND UPSTREAM'S PIN IS THE SHARPER HALF OF
IT** -- `238f719f50`, contained in `meq-integration` at `5c2324e921`. Their
tree's single-precision unit tests SKIP, so a single-precision defect has no
single-precision test to catch it; they put a DOUBLE into the same position
instead -- a tolerance no double bracket can reach, `1e-30`, a cap of 10,000,
and a COUNT of level-set calls rather than a clock -- and it reads **10,002
calls before the fix and under 100 after**, with a second section checking the
`1e-13` default still stops at its bracket. *A format-specific defect is pinned
by putting the other format in the same position*, which costs one test case
where a second build costs an install.

**THE BASELINE NEEDED NO STASH AND NO WORKTREE, WHICH IS THE CHEAP HALF**: the
pre-change state IS `pathTolerance()` returning `1e-13`, because `1e-13` is the
default, so one constant reproduces it exactly and the arm is controlled. *A
cure measured after changing two things attributes nothing* --
[M-210](#m-210) -- and this entry's first version changed MEQ's tolerance and
the MFEM install together and credited the tolerance.

### M-236

**A COARSE BORDERED SOLVE THAT DIVERGES IN SINGLE AND CONVERGES IN DOUBLE, AND
BOTH BUILDS FAIL IN THE SAME BAND 0.13 PER CENT AWAY -- M-186'S COIN TOSS ON A
FIFTH CASE, WITH THE MECHANISM NAMED THIS TIME.**

`PlasmaConnectivity`'s `run( 0, 1.15, 150 )`: the 314-element half-disc machine,
limiter radius 1.15. Double converges in 17 Newton iterations; single runs its
full 150 with the residual RISING, and the obvious reading -- a single-precision
defect -- is wrong.

**THE FIRST HALF IS M-186'S INSTRUMENT.** `MKL_NUM_THREADS` reassociates a
blocked BLAS-3 and changes nothing else, applied to one binary:

| MKL | single | its | `psi_ax` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1, 2 | **fails at the cap** | 150 | 2.915004e-02 |
| 3 | **fails at the cap** | 150 | 4.075228e-02 |
| 4 | converged | 11 | 1.170586362e-02 |
| 6 | converged | 11 | **1.170591858e-02** |
| 8, 16 | converged | 11 | 1.170589257e-02 |

Double reads `1.170592059e-02`. **At six MKL threads the single build reaches it
in ELEVEN iterations against double's seventeen**, agreeing to seven significant
figures. `tests/CMakeLists.txt` pins `MKL_NUM_THREADS = 1`, which is one draw.

**AND THE SECOND HALF IS WHAT MAKES IT A COIN TOSS RATHER THAN A FORMAT
VERDICT: THE DOUBLE BUILD FAILS HERE TOO.** A dense limiter sweep at the same
mesh, 61 radii over `1.1400` to `1.1700` in double at `MKL = 1`, has two
outright failures -- **1.1515 and 1.1695** -- two 48-iteration runs, and counts
bouncing 8 to 24, against a stable 9 to 11 everywhere outside the band. Checked
independently on the same binary at two radii 0.13 per cent apart:

| double, `n = 314` | |
|---|---|
| limiter `1.1500` | converges, 17 its, `psi_ax = 1.170592059e-02` |
| limiter `1.1515` | **`the non-linear iteration did not converge`**, 150 its |

**THE FAILURE SETS ARE INTERLEAVED**, which is the clincher -- 1.1500 is in
single's and 1.1515 is in double's:

| limiter | double | single |
|---|---|---|
| 1.1450 | 17 | 10 |
| 1.1475 | 11 | 18 |
| **1.1500** | **17** | **FAIL** |
| **1.1515** | **FAIL** | **9** |
| 1.1525 | 9 | 9 |
| 1.1600 | 10 | 29 |

*Neither build is the bad one.* Outside the band they are the same solver:
1.10/1.12/1.14/1.18 give 11/9/10/10 in double and 11/8/10/11 in single, and the
finer meshes give 10/8 against 9/7.

**THEY PART AT STEP 1 THROUGH THE LINE SEARCH AND NOT THROUGH THE ARITHMETIC**,
which is the part worth keeping. Step 0 is near-identical -- `fieldNorm`
1.240239e-01 against 1.240240e-01, the same `directionNorm`, both failing Armijo
on all twelve rungs and taking the `bestDamping` fallback at 0.5 -- but step 0's
trial ladder is a **sharp V**: double reads 59.71 at damping 1, **0.1885 at
0.5**, 2.352 at 0.25. Single reads 62.61, **0.1758**, 2.379. *Near the bottom of
a V a 3e-05 difference becomes 7 per cent*, and at step 1 double's full step is
rejected at merit 3.365e-01 where single's is accepted at 8.527e-02. Different
trajectories from there.

**AND THE DIVERGENCE IS THE AXIS ROW CLIMBING, NOT THE FIELD.** Single spends
**142 consecutive steps** at `damping = 2^-11`, `trials = 12`, `armijo = 0` --
the `bestDamping` fallback, which its own doxygen says *"is NOT an Armijo step:
it is how the residual rises from one iteration to the next"*. Differentiating
the trial ladder, **134 of 148 steps have `d(merit)/da > 0`** against double's 1
of 12, while `d( ||R|| )/da` -- the FIELD block -- is **negative at every step in
both builds**. Decomposing the merit names the row:

| step | field | **axis** | current | boundary | exterior |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | -5.93e-03 | **-7.74e-02** | -4.92e-03 | +7.9e-06 | -3.9e-06 |
| 100 | -5.19e-03 | **+4.29e-01** | +8.2e-05 | +1.9e-05 | -8.6e-06 |
| 148 | -4.70e-03 | **+3.91e-01** | -9.63e-03 | -3.1e-06 | +3.1e-06 |

Two orders above every other row and driving `|axis|` AWAY from zero where the
linearisation demands it go to zero. **The field Jacobian is sound and the
bordered direction is an ASCENT direction for the augmented merit.** Double
shows the same pathology in the same band and merely does not get absorbed by
it -- 1/10 ascent steps at `L = 1.145`, 2/12 at 1.149, 3/18 at 1.153 -- so the
stretch is a property of the PROBLEM at this resolution and radius, and the
format only decides whether the iteration escapes.

**WHAT WAS RULED OUT, EACH BY MEASUREMENT.** The differenced border columns are
**not reached at all**: `NormalisedMHDSource::normalisationDerivatives()`
returns `true` unconditionally, so the `psi_ax`, `psi_bnd` and current columns
are ANALYTIC on this fixture and the finite-difference fallback never runs --
which kills the first and most plausible suspect outright. `extensionFdStep()`
is not it either: the exterior transmission residual is 2e-08 in single against
a merit of 1e-02. M-187's zero-column species is impossible with the field block
descending at every one of 148 steps. It is not a tolerance -- the target is
1.19e-06 and the run sits at 1.16e-02 -- and not a floor, the best residual
being 5.47e-03 at **1212x** `convergedResidualFloor()`. It is not the starting
point: double survives a relative perturbation of the guess from 1e-12 to
**1e-03**, four orders ABOVE float epsilon, converging to nine digits every
time. And MEQ's two existing levers do not rescue it -- `setLineSearchMerit(
Field )` takes double from 17 to 11 and leaves single at the cap, and
`BorderedPicardThenNewton` fails at 300.

**NOTHING IS OWED FOR CORRECTNESS**: the run throws and the driver exits 2, so
no wrong answer is reported. What is owed is M-186's standing note on a fifth
case, and a test may not take *"this mesh converged"* as a hard precondition
there.

**AND IT IS THE MEASUREMENT `residualCollinearity` WAS WAITING FOR.** That
field's doxygen says *"RECORDED AND NOT ACTED ON ... Measure before remedying"*
(`GradShafranov.hpp:4153`). This run is the measurement: **`1.0000e+00` for 142
consecutive steps**, every one with `armijo = 0`, `trials = 12` and
`damping = 2^-11` -- about 1,700 residual evaluations and 142 Jacobian
assemblies spent after the iteration had demonstrably stopped moving, where
`freegsnke`'s own threshold is 0.9. An exit on *"collinearity above 0.9 and
Armijo failed for N consecutive steps"* turns 150 wasted iterations into an
early and honest failure. **It would not make this case converge**, and it must
not move any run that converges today, so it is a cost-and-diagnosis item rather
than a correctness one -- and the cost is concrete: this one row is most of
`PlasmaConnectivity`'s single-precision runtime.

### M-237

**THE TEN HOST READERS OF THE ITERATE ARE PORTED, THE GATES OPEN ON THEIR OWN
ONCE THE COLUMNS ARE DEVICE-CAPABLE -- AND THE BUS SAYS MEQ'S OWN READERS WERE
UNDER ONE PER CENT OF IT.**

**THE TEN WERE FOUND BY WATCHING THE ITERATE'S OWN BUFFER**, not by reading the
plan's list: a temporary probe in `countedHostRead()` tallied every funnel whose
data pointer was `solution`'s, on `machine-f-diiid` under `--device cuda` with
`MEQ_AXIS_DEVICE=force`. It named exactly ten sites, which is the plan's count:

| site | funnels of the iterate, per run |
|---|---|
| `CompressedRows::gather()`, the transmission constraint | 160 |
| `assemblePlasmaCurrent()` | 25 |
| `assembleNormalisationColumn()`, axis and boundary | 24 |
| `limiterValue()`, the `psi_bnd` row | 16 |
| `assembleCurrentColumn()`, `assembleCurrentRow()`, `assembleCurrentNormalisationCorner()` | 12 each |
| the bordered step's `savedState` copy | 12 |
| the exterior columns' `savedIterate` copy, the cold state's copy | 3 each |

**TEN ON THIS CASE, AND FOUR MORE THAT IT NEVER REACHES.** The probe can only
name what the run executes, and `machine-f-diiid` takes none of: `peakAt()`'s
nodal-maximum fallback, which runs when no axis is located and which the plan
listed among its ten; `limiterPolygonMaximum()` under
`LimiterConstraint::LocatedContact`, a search over the limiter's faces;
`projectUpDown()` under `UpDownSymmetry`; and `refreshPlasmaComponent()` under a
moving support. All four still read the iterate on the host and are not
ported. `recoverPeak()` and `totalPotential()` read it too, once, after a solve.

Every one of the ten now has a device route behind the axis route's gate --
`meq::DevicePlasmaLoops` for the five element loops, `meq::DeviceRows::dotAll()`
for the transmission rows, `meq::orderedDotOnDevice()` for the `psi_bnd` row,
and for the copies nothing but the funnel left out, a copy of a device-valid
vector being born device-valid ([M-205](#m-205)); the cold state's mask is
`meq::copyEntriesOnDevice()`. `src/meq/ResidentIterate.hpp`.

**FORCED, THE ITERATE NO LONGER CROSSES IN PHASE C.** Same run, same file:

| `--device cuda`, forced | phase C down | MB | phase C up | MB | the iterate read on the host |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before ([M-232](#m-232)) | 66 | 15.0 | 17 | -- | ten sites, every step |
| after | 150 | **2.13** | 64 | 1.11 | `downloadSolution()` only -- phase D |

`6 + 129` routes taken, 0 declined; `psi_ax`, `psi_bnd`, the X-point and the
Newton count to every printed digit of the host's. **The COUNT rose and the
BYTES fell sevenfold**, and both are honest: what is left in phase C is what
the host's control flow consumes -- per-element partials for `I_p` and its
corner (37 KB a call, summed on the host in element order for the reason
`assemblePlasmaCurrent()` gives), the ten transmission dots, the one `psi_bnd`
scalar, the axis candidates, and a support's worth of the current row. A batched
download per evaluation is the shape that would take the count down; it is not
built.

**TO THE BIT, AFTER ONE HERMITE DERIVATIVE WAS WRITTEN THE HOST'S WAY.** Each
route was run beside its host loop on the same state, in the forced run: the
plasma current, the current column, the transmission dots and the `psi_bnd` row
agreed to the bit at every call, and every route that carries a PROFILE
DERIVATIVE did not -- the row 818 of 109,203 entries off by up to 5.6e-17 on
3.1e-02, the corner 3.6e-15 on 9.5. `meq::hermite10Prime()` was
`( 3t - 1 )( t - 1 )` where `Profiles.cpp` writes `3t^2 - 4t + 1`, and the
profile scale multiplied before the division where `meq::ScaledProfile::prime()`
multiplies after. Both rewritten: **126 of 126 evaluations equal**. The
radii and weights are the host's own `Transform()` and `Weight()` values,
uploaded once, and the device file has `-fmad=false`, which is what makes that
reachable at all. `ResidentIterateTests` pins all six quantities and the three
small kernels to the bit under `debug` and `cuda`, and goes red in four places
with the factored derivative put back. *`SourceViewTests` could not see it*: it
admits `dF/dpsi` anywhere in the envelope of four ulps of `psi`, which is
correct for a knot and wide enough for a rounding.

**AND THE CONTROLS.** Forced under `--device debug`: exit 0 in 7 m 59 s, no
fault, the same answer -- every buffer the routes leave device-valid is
funnelled before a host read. Unforced, every gate stays shut (`0 taken`) and
the host path is the host path: `--device cpu` prints byte-for-byte what `HEAD`
prints, and `--device cuda` differs only in the last residual, 2.992853e-12
against `HEAD`'s own 2.992878, 2.993187 and 2.993032 over three runs -- cuDSS
([M-229](#m-229)). `DeviceParity` carries a forced CUDA arm from here on.

**THE FORCE SWITCH WAS FORCING THE WRONG VECTORS, AND IT COST 37.5 MB.**
`limiterValue()` is the `psi_bnd` row and is applied to the backsolved
DIRECTIONS as well as to the iterate; forcing every vector it was handed
uploaded each host-only direction to dot six entries of it -- 45 uploads. The
switch stands in for *the iterate is resident*, not *every vector is*, so the
directions are gated on their own flags (`vectorIsResident()`).

**THE PLAN SAID THE LAST READER WOULD TURN EVERY GATE ON, AND IT DID NOT.**
Unforced, all routes read `0 taken`: the gate wants the iterate `H- D+`, and the
Newton update adds HOST-ONLY columns into it. Re-running [M-229](#m-229)'s
experiment -- `UseDevice( true )` on `y`, `z`, `zL`, `zB` and each `exteriorZ`,
nothing forced -- **the gates open by themselves**: 6 axis and 118 iterate
routes taken, 0 declined, every printed digit the host's, and MEQ's counter
reads phase C at 138 down and 1.97 MB where M-229 read 20 transfers and
15.1 MB with the iterate dragged back every step. *Removing the readers is what
makes the columns worth moving; it does not move them.* The experiment is
reverted, for the reason below.

**AND THE BUS SAYS MEQ'S COUNTER SEES UNDER ONE PER CENT OF IT.**
`nsys profile --trace=cuda` over the whole run, MB / count:

| arm | host to device | device to host |
|---|---|---|
| plain | 692 / 1449 | 259 / 918 |
| forced | 692 / 1433 | 409 / 1312 |
| columns resident | 731 / 1482 | 442 / 1329 |

The plain arm's counter reads **0.888 MB** of that. A `gdb` breakpoint on
`mfem::CuMemcpyDtoH` with a backtrace per hit attributes the device-to-host
side, and the largest item is not MEQ's code:

| where | plain | columns resident |
|---|---|---|
| `DarcyNPCSolver::ArrayMult` > `BlockVector::SyncFromBlocks` | **504, 140 MB** | 504, 140 MB |
| `DarcyNPCSolver::ArrayMult`, directly | -- | **168, 140 MB** |
| `SyncFromBlocks`, other callers | 79, 22.5 MB | 147, 45.1 MB |
| `DarcyHybridization::NonlinearResidualFinish` | 56, 18.6 MB | 56, 18.6 MB |
| `LinearForm::Assemble` in `prepare()` | 17, 7.6 MB | 17, 7.6 MB |
| `DarcyHybridization::NPCResidualFinish` | 20, 3.4 MB | 20, 3.4 MB |

**EVERY BACKSOLVED COLUMN IS DOWNLOADED INSIDE UPSTREAM'S BLOCKED SOLVE, ON
TODAY'S DEFAULT PATH.** `ArrayMult` writes each column's three blocks through a
`BlockVector` over `Y[ j ]` -- on the device, `NPCRecover` being a kernel -- and
then calls `SyncFromBlocks()`, which is `block.SyncAlias( base )`: it makes each
BLOCK match the BASE, and MEQ hands it a base that is host-valid, so each block
is copied down. **Per Newton step that is 14 columns** -- the field direction
`y`, the three border columns `z`, `zB` and `zL`, and the ten exterior modes;
XP-3's two cost no column -- so 11.7 MB a step, and over the run's twelve steps
(sweeps of 7, 3 and 2) 168 columns, three blocks each, 140 MB. A fixed-boundary
case with only the `psi_ax` border pays for two columns a step. That also qualifies
[M-227](#m-227)'s reading, which was that the columns read `H+ D-` at the flush
because they were never on the device: measured here under cuDSS they are
produced there and brought down by this call, and under M-227's PARDISO the
flux and potential blocks come out of the same `NPCRecover` kernel -- not
re-measured, so *qualifies* rather than *corrects*. A
device-capable column (`UseDevice( true )`) that still arrives host-valid pays a
SECOND full download per column, which is the experiment's extra 168. So the
columns item is now precise: the outputs must arrive DEVICE-valid at
`ArrayMult()` and the border's dense algebra must read them there -- the
`deviceDots` route, built in [M-208](#m-208) -- or the 140 MB stays.

**AND PHASE D DOWNLOADS THE ANSWER TWICE.** `downloadSolution()` funnels the
state and then its three long-lived aliases, and each alias, still flagged
device-valid, copies its own range again: 12 transfers and 5.0 MB over three
solves where 2.5 MB would do. A `SyncAliasMemory()` from the base after the one
read is the repair. Small, and recorded rather than built.

*An instrument that counts one project's funnels measures that project's
readers, not the bus.* The counter was right about everything it could see,
and the ten readers it saw were real -- and the largest single transfer in a
device run of MEQ was one call further in, in a library routine it does not
instrument. `nsys` and a breakpoint on MFEM's own copy are the instruments for
the bus; the counter remains the one for attribution inside MEQ.

### M-238

**THE BORDERED COLUMNS STAY ON THE DEVICE, AND THE BUS SAYS SO: DEVICE-TO-HOST
FROM 259 MB TO 101 MB, HOST-TO-DEVICE FROM 692 MB TO 543 MB, WITH THE HOST'S
ANSWER TO EVERY PRINTED DIGIT ON 27 OF THE 29 SHIPPED EXAMPLES.**

The columns are fourteen a Newton step on `machine-f-diiid` -- the field
direction `y`, the three border columns `z`, `zB` and `zL`, and ten exterior
modes; XP-3's two cost no backsolve -- so 168 over the run's twelve steps.
Each change was found by attributing the bus rather than by reading a counter:
`nsys` for the totals, a `gdb` breakpoint on MFEM's own copy for the call sites
([M-237](#m-237)).

| after | device to host | host to device |
|---|---|---|
| `machine-f-diiid`, `--device cuda`, whole run, before | 259 MB / 918 | 692 MB / 1449 |
| `flush()` makes each output device-valid before `ArrayMult()`, and the dense fill contracts every row against every column in ONE launch | 148 MB / 669 | 658 MB / 1446 |
| `DeviceNPCOperator::Mult()` makes `y` and `xLoc` device-valid | 101 MB / 524 | 623 MB / 1340 |
| the ten exterior columns go up once per solve, in phase B | **101 MB / 522** | **543 MB / 1008** |

The first row removed `ArrayMult()`'s 504 downloads (140 MB) and exposed the
residual's: with the iterate resident, `DeviceNPCOperator::Mult()`'s own
`SyncFromBlocks()` calls grew from 79 copies to 147, which the second row
removes.

**ONE MISTAKE, FOUR TIMES: `BlockVector::SyncFromBlocks()` MAKES EACH BLOCK
MATCH ITS BASE.** It is `block.SyncAlias( base )`, and `SyncAlias_` copies the
block's other copy across wherever the base says a location is live. Every
site above handed a kernel's output a base that said HOST -- a fresh
`mfem::Vector v( n )`, or a scratch vector after `Update()` -- so every block a
kernel wrote was copied straight back down. `ArrayMult()` did it to the
columns, MEQ's own residual did it to the residual and to `xLoc`, and MEQ's own
comment on that residual said the call *carries the blocks up*. **The repair is
`Write()` on the base before the blocks are written** -- it moves nothing and
marks the device copy live -- and, where a scratch vector's blocks were made
before it was device-capable, `UseDevice( true )` on each block by name:
`mfem::Device( "debug" )` faulted in a host `memcpy` there, because
`Vector::operator=` runs where either side's flag says and `Update()` at an
unchanged size keeps the blocks it made first. Under CUDA that same copy was a
silent host write repaired by an upload.

**THE FILL IS BIT-IDENTICAL TO THE HOST `rowDot()` AND ITS DISPATCH WAS
CHECKED ENTRY BY ENTRY.** Every border row is `meq::RowView` -- the compressed
transmission and current rows from their mirrors, `psi_ax`'s, `psi_bnd`'s and
XP-3's from a small table rebuilt per fill -- and one thread per `( row,
column )` sums from zero in the host's order, in the file compiled without FMA.
A temporary probe ran the host `rowDot()` beside every entry: **240 of 240 a
step equal**, over all twelve steps, after one correction. XP-3's `total -= w v`
folds into its weights exactly, IEEE subtraction being addition of the
negation; `psi_bnd`'s `-limiterValue( v )` does NOT, because `-( +0 )` is `-0`
and a sum of negated terms from `+0` is `+0`. The probe met that twice a step
against the X-point's zero columns, and the general case -- a nonzero column
whose entries at the contact happen to vanish -- is why `meq::RowView` carries
a `negate` flag rather than the special case alone. `DeviceRowsTests` pins all
three arms, signed zero included.

**AND THE ONE-ROW BORDER TOO, WHICH IS EVERY FIXED-BOUNDARY MACHINE.** Its
columns are `y` and `z` and its elimination is a division, which read them on
the host -- so on `fixed-a-testtokamak` every route stayed declined. The same
launch serves it: 10 axis evaluations and 7 iterate readers on the device, the
host's `psi_ax` and Newton count. On `ff3` the axis leg reads 22.1 s against
M-235's 33.6 s, and **21.9 s of it is ONE cold sweep** -- the solve's first
evaluation, made before the iterate has ever been on the device; the other
fifteen take 0.19 s between them.

**AND THE ROUTES NOW OPEN WITHOUT BEING FORCED.** Under `--device cuda` on
`machine-f-diiid`, with nothing set: 6 axis and X-point evaluations and 118
iterate readers on the device, 0 declined, the bordered row dots on the device,
and MEQ's host funnels down from about 10,500 to 460 a run. The host path is
byte-identical to what it printed before.

**AND OPENING THE ONE-ROW BORDER EXPOSED THE AXIS ROUTES' ONE SEMANTIC
DIFFERENCE ON A SHIPPED CASE.** `rotating-normalised` reads `psi_ax =
1.039297e-01` under CUDA and under `debug` alike -- so not a stale read --
against the host's `1.039325e-01`, same seven Newton steps, parting at step 3.
Both report the axis LOCATED; they located different points. The device's is
the root the post-solve check also finds, at `( 1.0919, 0 )` and normalised
flux 1.0000; the host's warm ring walk settles on a point whose flux sits above
it, and its own post-solve check then reads normalised flux 0.9999. That is the
difference `AxisSearch.hpp` states and leaves to `DeviceParity` -- nearest
clean root globally against the first productive ring -- and `DeviceParity`'s
cases had never met it, the two-row borders having agreed throughout. It is a
768-element rectangle, the coarsest case in the tree. **Owed: which of the two
the constraint should take**, and the device's is the one the run's own check
agrees with.

**27 OF 29 SHIPPED EXAMPLES GIVE THE HOST'S ANSWER UNDER CUDA: `rotating-
normalised` IS THE ONE ABOVE, AND `diverted-tokamak` WAS ALREADY WRONG.** `psi_ax`, `psi_bnd`, the X-point and the Newton count compared
as printed text, cpu against cuda: every multi-row bordered machine, the
`q(psi)`-driven outer loop, `rotating-rectangle` and the fixed-boundary six --
whose one-row border now runs on the device too -- agree; `manufactured` exits
1 on both. **`diverted-tokamak` does not**: the host
converges in 25 steps to `psi_ax = 8.486e-02`, this tree under CUDA in 11 to

too**, in 55 steps to `psi_ax = -8.206e-02`, which the driver refuses. The two
part from the host at the FIRST Newton step, by far more than round-off. It is
the only shipped case with a MOVING plasma support and a prescribed limiter, and
`DeviceParity` covers neither; the likeliest mechanism is the device integrand
reading XP-1's element flags as of its last rebuild while
`refreshPlasmaComponent()` moves the mask every residual. That was it, and it is
fixed -- [M-239](#m-239).

**AND THE OUTPUT STAGE OF A CURVED FIXED-BOUNDARY CASE COULD NOT RUN UNDER
`debug` AT ALL.** `HEAD` faults on `fixed-a-testtokamak` before the solve; with
the routes open the solve completes and `meq::curveBoundaryOnto()` faults
twice -- a copy of the mesh nodes born device-valid, then a device-aware

of the nodes while the flags named the device's; whether the `.vtu` writer then
read the un-bent copy was not checked.

**WHAT IS LEFT ON THE BUS IS UPSTREAM'S, AND IT IS MOSTLY SCRATCH.** Of the

`MultNL()`, `GetSubVector`, `NPCResidualFinish`. MEQ's own share is the phase-C
partials and scalars (2 MB) and phase D's answer, which `downloadSolution()`

### M-239

**`diverted-tokamak` HAD FOUR FAILURE MODES ON RECORD OR IN THE TREE, AND THEY
ARE FOUR DIFFERENT THINGS: ONE DEVICE DEFECT, NOW FIXED; ONE CURE NOBODY HAD
RECORDED; ONE LIMIT OF THE FORMULATION; AND A SHIPPED EXAMPLE THAT REPORTS THE
BRANCH ITS OWN HEADER DOES NOT COMPARE AGAINST.**

The case is the only shipped one with a MOVING plasma support -- `ConfineToPlasma`
with no X-point border and no `PlasmaSupportSweeps`, so `refreshPlasmaComponent()`
re-decides the support at every residual -- and its `psi_bnd` is a point limiter
at freegs4e's X-point.

**1. UNDER ANY DEVICE THE INTEGRAND READ A STALE SUPPORT. FIXED.** The device
integrand's element flags are an upload in `npcConstants`, refreshed only when
the NPC operator is rebuilt; the host's `meq::SourceIntegrator` reads the live
mask. So the two integrated `F` over different supports from the first time the
support moved -- the first Newton step. Measured on one binary:

| arm | Newton | `psi_ax` | first `‖r‖` | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| host, `MKL_NUM_THREADS` 1, 2, 4, 8; 4 OpenMP threads; UMFPACK; batched local factorisation | 25 | 8.486305e-02 | 6.844383e-02 | all seven identical |
| `cuda`: cuDSS or PARDISO, serial or batched local factorisation | 11 | 8.091091e-02 | 6.858029e-02 | all four identical, axis INSIDE coil P1U |
| `debug`, host arithmetic | 11 | 8.091091e-02 | 6.858029e-02 | the same wrong answer |
| `HEAD`, `cuda` | 55 | **-8.205878e-02** | | refused by the driver |
| `HEAD` single, `cuda` | 49 | **-8.205861e-02** | | refused |
| **fixed**, `cuda` | **25** | **8.486305e-02** | **6.844383e-02** | the host's to every printed digit |
| **fixed**, single `cuda` | 23 | 8.486282e-02 | | single host's to its floor |

*Seven host perturbations agreeing exactly and four device arms agreeing exactly
with each other but not with the host* is what said "semantic, not arithmetic"
before any code was read, and `debug` reproducing the card's answer to every
digit said it again. `refreshPlasmaComponent()` now carries every move to the
uploaded flags -- comparison inside `DeviceConstants::refresh()` keeps an
unmoved mask free -- through one `deviceIntegrandInputs()` shared with the
operator's build. **`DeviceParity` could not see it**: both its cases freeze the
support within a solve. It now runs this case on `cpu`, `cuda` and forced
`cuda`, without the `debug` arm, which the defect does not need.

**2. SINGLE PRECISION NO LONGER FAILS, AND THE CURE PREDATES THIS WORK.**
[M-221](#m-221) recorded a singular border at `MKL_NUM_THREADS = 1` and a
refused negative-`psi_bnd` branch at 2, 4 and 8. Today, and at `HEAD`, the
single build converges at all four in 23 steps to `psi_ax = 8.48628e-02`, within
FP32's floor of double's. Several things landed between M-221 and `HEAD` --
[M-222](#m-222)'s inverse-transform tolerance and marking offset among them --
and none is credited: the old binary is gone, and *a cure measured after
changing several things attributes nothing*.

**3. A COLD START IS SINGULAR, ON EVERY ARM, AND THAT IS THE FORMULATION.**
Without `[initialguess]` the zero Dirichlet datum makes the cold iterate
`psi_h = 0`, the support is empty, and the plasma-current row of the dense
corner is identically zero -- `|row| 0.000e+00`, on the host and the card
alike, through Newton and Picard-then-Newton both. The trivial branch every
GS-2 source has (`CLAUDE.md`, *Traps*), met through the current constraint. The
example ships a warm start for this reason.

**4. AND THE SHIPPED EXAMPLE REPORTS THE OTHER BRANCH.** [M-132](#m-132)
established that this prescribed-limiter formulation has discrete equilibria
selected by the starting `psi_bnd`: from 0 it reaches `8.486e-02`, seeded near
the answer it reaches `8.266e-02`, and the two do not merge under refinement.
The file starts from 0, so it reports `8.486305e-02` -- **2.6% from the
freegs4e `psi_axis` its own header lists "for anything comparing against
it"**. Freezing the support within each solve selects the benchmarked branch:

| `diverted-tokamak`, `k = 2`, 2642 elements | Newton | `psi_ax` | `psi_bnd` |
|---|---|---|---|
| as shipped, the support moving inside Newton | 25 | 8.486305e-02 | 3.229767e-02 |
| `PlasmaSupportSweeps = 4`, host and `cuda` alike | 7 + 3 + 2 | **8.266088e-02** | **3.237970e-02** |
| `diverted-tokamak-xpoint`, the X-point a border ([M-87](#m-87)) | | 8.266004e-02 | 3.237932e-02 |
| freegs4e, 129^2 | | 8.271751e-02 | 3.240413e-02 |

The moving support's own Jacobian is not the problem: both profiles vanish
quadratically at `Psi_N = 0`, so the edge term `dF/dpsi` cannot carry is zero.
The slow phase is globalisation -- the step-0 full Newton step is 249 times
WORSE in merit, and the line search accepts a sixteenth to a half of a step for
fifteen steps before the quadratic finish. **The example now sets
`PlasmaSupportSweeps = 4`**, decided as a change of which equilibrium it reports
rather than made silently, and its header's comparison holds: `8.266088e-02` on
host and `cuda` alike, in 7 + 3 + 2 steps. `DeviceParity` keeps the moving
support covered by running a copy with that key stripped -- no other shipped
example moves a FILLED support.

### M-240

**THE FIRST EVALUATION OF A SOLVE IS ON THE DEVICE, AND WHAT KEPT IT OFF WAS A
QUADRATIC MERGE -- NOT THE HOST, NOT THE ROOTING, AND NOT WHERE THE ITERATE
WAS.**

[M-238](#m-238) left `ff3`'s axis leg at 22.1 s, 21.9 of it one cold sweep, and
`DEVICE-PLAN.md` read it as the iterate starting host-valid while every gate
wants it device-only. **Uploading the iterate once, ahead of its first reader,
was necessary and on its own made things WORSE**: the device route still
declined, and the host sweep that replaced it now downloaded the iterate it had
just been sent -- phase C from 0.001 MB to 35.3. *A crossing moved earlier is
still a crossing until its reader moves too.*
Probed rather than argued, the refusal was the candidate ceiling -- **4,960
candidates on `fixed-a-testtokamak`'s 2,480 elements**, two per element. A
`Type = "ramp"` guess seeds the potential and the trace and leaves the flux
block zero, so `q_h` is identically zero, `max | q |` is zero, the stopping rule
is absolute, and every element meets it at its own seed. Every
`examples/fixed-*.toml` starts there.

**AND `perf` PUT THE 22 SECONDS IN THE MERGE.** On `ff3` under CUDA,
`CriticalPointFinder::mergeCandidates()` is **13.9% of a 156 s run** -- the
whole leg -- and the rooting beside it does not rank. The merge walked the kept
list for every candidate, and on a list of two hundred thousand nearly all kept
that is quadratic. *A cost attributed to a route is a cost of the route only if
the other route does not pay it*: the host sweep calls the same merge.

| `ff3`, `--device cuda`, `OMP = MKL = 1` | M-238 | upload only | **all four** |
|---|---|---|---|
| solve | 43.3 s | 41.1 s | **21.7 -- 22.9 s** |
| axis leg | 22.1 s | 19.8 s | **0.40 -- 0.42 s** |
| cold full sweeps on the host | 1 | 1 | **0** |
| axis and X-point evaluations on device | 23 taken, 1 declined | 23, 1 | **24, 0** |
| phase C down | 0.001 MB | 35.3 MB | **1.57 MB** |
| Newton history | | | M-238's run's to iteration 9; iteration 10 at cuDSS's 1e-15 |

**The four, and each is necessary:**

1. **The iterate goes up once, before its first reader**, under `Phase::Upload`:
   `countedDeviceReadWrite()`, a new funnel, because a `Read()` leaves the host
   copy valid and opens no gate.
2. **`mergeCandidates()` is grid-indexed** and returns the walk's list **to the
   bit**. Every point that can match lies within `max( separation x diameter,
   largest reach )`, so a grid of that cell size holds every candidate match in
   the 3 x 3 block around it, and the smallest matching index there is the
   index the walk stopped at; a replacement moves its point on the grid.
   `theMergeIsTheWalkItReplaces` holds the walk verbatim as the oracle on 6,400
   candidates reaching all three branches -- 524 separated, 928 replaced -- and
   goes red at 4,453 kept against 3,846 with the search narrowed to one cell.
3. **The candidate ceiling is gone.** The list is at most two per element by
   construction, so the mesh bounds it, and at the bound it is the size of the
   iterate; a refusal cost the iterate's download PLUS a host sweep.
   `itReturnsTheWholeCandidateListHoweverLong` takes 10,000 roots off a
   zero-flux fixture and matches the host sweep element for element.
4. **The nodal fallback runs on the device.** No candidate on a zero-flux field
   is an axis, so `peakAt()` falls back to the largest potential dof -- and that
   walk downloaded the iterate, 17.7 MB, and the cold-state copy after it a
   second time. Two exact reductions replace it: `fmax`, then the smallest
   index holding the maximum, which is the walk's first-of-equals.
   **`mfem::ArgMaxReducer` was the obvious primitive and is wrong**: its `Join`
   is `a.first <= b.first`, so a tie goes to whichever joined last.
   `theNodalPeakIsTheWalk` pins ties, NaN, signed zero and an all `-inf` range,
   and goes red with the index match loosened.

**AND FIVE DOWNLOADS AND UPLOADS ELSEWHERE WERE MEQ'S OWN.** `machine-f-diiid`
under CUDA, `nsys` over the whole run:

| | M-238 | now |
|---|---|---|
| host to device | 543.4 MB, 1,008 copies | **508.2 MB, 909** |
| device to host | 100.7 MB, 522 | **78.6 MB, 470** |

* **Phase D downloaded the answer twice.** `downloadSolution()` funnelled the
  base and then each of its three aliases, whose flags still said device-only
  -- so each copied its block down again. `SyncMemory()` copies flags and
  nothing else, and after the base's download the flags are true of the
  aliases: `ff3` 35.3 MB to 17.7.
* **`curveBoundaryOnto()` restored the nodes with a device-aware `=`** eight
  times, so the funnel after each brought them back: 25.2 MB on `ff3`, the
  funnel M-238 added to fix a `debug` fault. A host copy is what every reader
  wanted.
* **`fluxGf = darcyFlux; fluxGf.Neg()` ran on the device** after the flux had
  just come down, and the post-solve axis check's finder downloaded it again:
  9.42 MB on `ff3`. Written as `-x` on the host, the same bits.
* **`DeviceNPCOperator::Mult`'s `rLoc` arrived host-valid**, so upstream's
  residual finish synced its device-written blocks down to it and the copies
  into the output put them back up: 28 a run each way. Upstream named this in
  its reply -- *MEQ's `r` has `UseDevice()` false* -- and it is `xLoc`'s repair
  again.

**`DEVICE-PLAN.md`'s item 2 WAS MISATTRIBUTED, AND THE CONTROL IS WHAT SAID
SO.** It read the per-residual uploads under `ResidualRowsBatched()` as MEQ's
`darcyRhs`. Uploading `darcyRhs` once per rebuild added 11.2 MB and moved those
33 uploads not at all -- they are upstream's `darcy_u` and `darcy_p`, copied
from the state inside `NPCResidualStart()` -- so it was reverted. *A fix that
does not move the number it was written for is a measurement of the
attribution.* And a flag sync on `xLoc`'s blocks, found by a probe that showed
them `H1 D0` under a device-only base, moved nothing either and was reverted:
the copy runs on the source's flags, not the destination's.

**THE PHASE-C SCALARS ARE MEASURED AND LEFT.** 247 device-to-host copies of
4 KB or less over `machine-f-diiid`, **0.29 ms** of copy time in all. Batching
them is a restructuring of the step for well under one per cent.

**AND `machine-f-diiid` READS `3.759850e-01`, NOT THE `3.759851e-01` THIS FILE
QUOTES SIXTY TIMES** -- on the host and the card alike, at this change and in
the logs of the commit before it, with `psi_bnd` `7.081392e-02` and the X-point
`( 1.200929, -0.999490 )` one unit off in the last printed digit too. Nothing
